Live a life of integrity. Full vs marginal thinking. Never give in to “just this once”.  Ignore sunk costs. It’s tempting to think that you can leverage capital already gained to tackle new challenges, to incur a marginal cost, but you will end up paying the full cost anyway. 100% of the time is easier than 98% of the time. Don’t do it “just this once” for the “marginal cost.” life is one undending stream of extenuating circumstances.  It’s easier to hold to your principles 100% of the time than it is to hold to them 98% of the time. Your personal moral line is powerful because you don’t cross it.  When you justify once, there’s nothing to stop you doing it again.  Decide what you stand for, and then stand for it all the time.  Never start making moral concessions in your life.  Whether they want one or not, every company has a purpose. Some purposes are simply given by emergent strategies, but if a company has chosen a clearance compelling purpose, it's impact and legacy can be extraordinary. The purpose serves as a beacon.  The 3 parts of purpose: likeness: what you want something to become at the end of the path you are on. Commitment: to the likeness. Metrics: to measure your progress toward the likeness.  If you find that your likeness isn’t who you want to become, then revisit your likeness and decide who you truly want to be.  Constrained by our mind, we cannot always see the big picture. We need to aggregate to start to see it.  God doesn’t need to aggregate. His measure of achievement is the individual. The only metrics we need are the individuals we help in whatever assignment or role we may have.  The more i focused on my problems, the more I despaired. Take the time to figure out your life purpose. Clarity about purpose will trump other concerns in the long-run.

Title: Man’s search for meaning
Author: Viktor e frankl
Notes: Man does not simply exist, but decides next what he will be. A human being has freedom to take a stand toward conditions, but not freedom from conditions. Every human being has the freedom to change at any instant. We are capable of changing ourselves and other things for the better. How can we dare to predict the behavior of man? A human being is not one thing among others, not a machine. Man has potentialities. Man invented the gas chambers, and also yet is also they that entered the gas chambers uprightly with God on his lips. Tragic Optimism. How is it possible to say yes to life, in spite of “all that”? Make the best of any situation. Best as in optimal, or optimistic aim. A human being is not one in pursuit of happiness, but a reason to be happy. Happiness is not pursued, but ensued. The existential vacuum or collective neurosis of our time can be rightly described as a private and personal form of nihilism.  Psychotherapy can be problematic in it’s assertions, becoming a symptom of theass neurosis/nihilism and not a solution. For example, there is a danger in teaching that man is nothing but a product or result of environment and biology, that he is the victim of elements beyond his control or outside influences. This neurotic fatalism is fostered and strengthened by a psychotherapy that denies that man is free. Pandeterminism = the view of man that disregards his capacity to take a stand toward any conditions whatsoever. Man is not fully conditioned or determined, but rather determines himself  whether he gives in to conditions or stands up to them.  He decides what he will become in the next moment.  Freedom is in danger of  degenerating into mere arbitrariness unless it is lived in terms of responsibleness.  If a human is not more than a damaged brain machine, for what purpose should people serve as psychiatrists or therapists? What man becomes, he has made of himself. Tragic triad = pain, guilt, death.    Saying yes to life, presupposes that life is potentially meaningful under any conditions, even those which are most miserable. What matters is to make the best of any situation.  Faith, love, and hope, cannot be ordered or forced.  The drug scene is one aspect of a more general phenomenon of  the feeling of meaningless resulting from the frustration of our existential needs.  People have enough to live by, but nothing to live for.  Man does not live by welfare alone.  Meaninglessness is the proof of one’s humanness, though it may cause a pathological reaction. Depression, aggression, addiction, are three facets of the mass neurotic syndrome. Not each and every case is a direct result of meaninglessness, but it may be overcome if there is a meaning worth living for.  Who can guarantee that a larger meaning will not present itself later on in your life? You will have to carry on and see in order to find out.  Meaning is changed by context, by each frame in a moving picture. The final meaning of life presents itself at the end, on the verge of death, it cannot be known now. Creating meaning in a life is done in one of three main ways: creating a work or doing a deed, experiencing something or encountering someone, to rise above or consider suffering enobling/enabling or turning predicaments into human achievements.  Meaning is down-to-earth, becoming aware as to what can be done about a situation. Conscience directs within a hiearchy of values, built in the evolution of our species.   One may find meaning in suffering. We benefit from captivity when we see it as a growth experience.  “I broke my neck, it didn’t break me”.  Without my suffering,  the growth I have achieved would have been impossible.  Meaning is available through suffering. Unnecessary suffering is masochistic.  We dehumanizing mistaken people or convicts, etc., by explaining their error and reasoning away the mystery of their mistake., seeing them as a machine to be fixed, rather than a free human. To be seen as a human who can choose wrong, and then rise above guilt and become a better person is more meaningful and empowering.  Collective guilt is totally irresponsible, to hold one person responsible for the behavior of another.   Live as if you are living for the second time, and acted as wrongly the first time as you are about to act now. Everything is errevocably  stored and treasured from the past, nothing lost.  Young people should envy the old, not pity them.  Our society adores the young, those who are “useful”. Nihilism does not contain that there isnnothing, but that everything is meaningless.  It is a learned meaninglessness.  Everything will bec9me still worse, unless each of us does his/her best.  Dostoevsky: am I worthy of my suffering? - What does life expect of me? Each is irreplaceable, with unique demands and abilities. Thus each has a distinct why for their life. A man who knows he bears responsibility toward something else has found his why, and cannot throw away his life, despite the how.

Title: The anxious generation
Author: Jonathan haidt
Notes:
What is anxiety: anticipation of future threat. When our anxiety alarm is triggered by ordinary events, this becomes a disorder. Adolescents are more worried about social death than physical death. Mdd: major depressive disorder. What changed during the early 2010s? Increased reports and different behavior tell us something happened. The great rewiring is what happened. Collective anxiety is empowering and energizing, but young people have learned to take it on alone in the virtual world. Sharing contagious emotions individually, not collectively. Free play is freely chosen and directed by the participants, engaged in for it’s own sake. Physical play is one of the best forms. Children can only learn how to not get hurt where there is the possibility of getting hurt.  Attunement between individuals is important. Social interactions are like tennis, it’s fun, you take turns, and timing is a necessary component. Synchrony is also an important game, in activities such as singing, creating community between individuals. Rituals like this are on all continents.  Synchronous face-to-face activities are part of our deep biological development/evolution. Digital interaction is unembodied, asynchronous, and not face-to-face.  Copying your parents is a losing strategy. Conformist bias and prestige bias. Conformity attraction or conformist bias is the pull to conform, similar to what we call peer pressure. Prestige is given by others to an individual who they deem to have done something with great excellence, a signal to the community of their standing. Social media gets children 
to conform and seek prestige.  Language learning is a sensitive period of development. 9-15 is a cultural sensitive period of development, the same years as puberty.  Handling this development of culture relationships and self online instead of offline is problematic.  Childhood is an apprenticeship to learn social interaction.  Frustrate your children by laying out the boundaries of life. They need this, because they are antifragile as they learn to deal with frustration and pain and emotional discomfort.  Real-world play should involve some risk. We don’t want scars, but we do want to see bruises.  Free unsupervised play is what helps children set their normal nervous system state to “discover mode”, because they see the opportunities around them in the world, and are not taught to see the world as unsafe.  Peoples around the world have had rites of passage, particularly at puberty. When there are no rites of passage, adolescents tend to make their own. They need a way to venture out into the world with peers, as a fully integrated individual. Children need rites of passage to organize their world. We have simple examples, such as pg-13 ratings, ordriving at 16, or access to bars at 21. Online, there are no age limits. On the internet, everyone is the same age, which is no particular age, there is no age or societal role on the internet. We want children to feel they are climbing a ladder with clearly defined rungs. They need shared standards, steps to take in their life. Smartphones and similar devices are experience-blockers, pushing out other activities and forms of play. They are like the cuckoo bird, that pushes out others from the nest.  Animal learning is the wearing smooth of a path in the brain ( a high learning curve, like a cat thrashing about to learn a pattern of reward, or a person in a trance tapping about mindlessl and habitually on a screen).  Around 2010, the usual social media network  became a social media platform, where relationships of one-to-many became much more common.  Harms from social media/etc. Use: social deprivation, sleep deprivation, attention deprivation, addiction/strong habits. Media multitasking is related to attention issues. Hooked model: trigger, action, invariable investment, trigger. Variable reward (maybe it will happen, maybe not) creates the strongest anticipation and habits. Investment is unique to human behaviorism,  or habit-forming behavior design. Dysphoria is the withdrawal of tech habitual use.  The benefits of social media do not seem to be real. The real world is always better than the internet.  The few plausible benefits do not outweigh the negatives for young teens.  The usual withdrawal symptoms (anxiety, irritability, insomnia, dysphoria). The syptoms of withdrawal from media use, are much like the withdrawal symptoms of slot machines.  By decreasing join laughter, eye contact, and conversational skills, social media negatively impacted even those who stayed away from it.  Social media isn’t just making girls depressed, it’s making them bit hype too, with more ways to shame and bully relationally, and do it anonymously, not face-to-face.   Happiness is contagious. Bad feelings are even more contagious. Women are also better at spreading these feelings. Thus, bad mental health spreads more quickly, and it spreads more between girls. Mass communication facilitates  the transmission of psychogenic illnesses. Two anxiety processes. Emotional contagion, and the prestige bias. Conformity bias is especially harmful when the audience is behaving unhealthily.   Odd ticks have spread through infouencers. Individuals have literally picked up twitches from people they follow.  Mentally unhealthy ideas spread and become popular. People tell their therapists they have certain issues, and they really don’t.   Gender dysphoria spreads similar.  Women get more unwanted sexual attention online. They get this even from male peers. Women are shamed for sending nudes, but male peers exploit it for their own desires. These girls feel they must do it in order to avoid being shunned.  Boys choose more agency activities, ways to make them stand out and fine their way in the world. Girls choose more communion activities, ways to connect emotionally with others.  Boys switched their time to online activities. Much like Japanese hermit boys. Their mental health declined by porn, addictions, and offering alternatives to real-life risk and difficulties that help them become adult men.  Anomi,  they end up feeling their lives are meaningless.  The divinity axis: somethings bring us closer to divinity or the feeling of such.  There is no sacred in the online world. Everything is always open, always available. There are no social rules, bounds on time and space, etc. No joint action and real connection between physical humans.  Our screens do not give us awe. We are not uplifted by social media.  We need to let kids do things on their own, play on their own, do tasks outside their comfort zone, try things we aren’t sure they can do, all on their own. They need phone-free schools.  Children need play, unsupervised. Become a playful school. Free play is nature’s way. Fewer rules are needed. Dkids need to do projects on their own.  “Parenting” was hardly a used word until the 1950s. In the 1970s, families changed, and the word “parenting” become popular. It became something people thought they should be trained for.  They began to rely on experts. Parents began to think like carpenters. Measure  twice, cut once. Parenting is better thought of as a gardener. It is messy, and is about creating a good space for children to flourish. We give them toys, we don’t tell them how to play.  Give kids free play, with age diversity, and a secure base to launch from. 0-18 months: video chat with a parent. 18-24 months: Ed programming with parent. 2-5 years. 1 hr weekdays, 3 hrs weekend. 6-older encourage healthy habits. Turn off screens during meals and outings. Use parental controls. Don’t use tech as pacifiers or babysitters or tantrum stoppers.   Letgrow.org. after school is for freeplay.  Go camping without tech. Your children will do what you do, not what you say. Make your neighborhood into a playborhood. Make it regular. Kids will come if other kids are there.  Commonsensemedia.com. use parental controls and filters. Have tech in open areas for children. It is possible to overprotective in the virtual world, especially when it becomes surveillance. Don’t monitor your child’s every move and private conversations, etc. Limits are hard to impose when you are the only ones enforcing them. Coordinate with other parents if needed. Remove all devices from private areas at a particular time at night. Watch for addictive or problematic habits with tech.  Behavior is problematic if it interferes with responsibilities, they experience strong cravings, they lieor deceive to get time online, they choose it over in-person activities often, it interferes withfriend relationships, it prevents them from getting needed hours of quality sleep, it prevents regular physical activity, they keep using social media even though they say they don’t want to. Talk to them a out it, and if needed do a digital detox. Delay accounts on social media until we'll into high school. Talk to your teens about the risks. Tell then about risks of setting, online media, truth, addictive behaviors, data use, etc.  Rely on your teens at home. Give them things to do and ways to help out. It gives them a team to be on, meaning and purpose in their life, a feeling of usefulness.  Give them ways to guide and lead and mentor younger kids.  Give them opportunities to stay away from home, such as backpacking and camping. Gove them a gap year after high school to help them live and understand life., work, and experience life and mature before starting university or such.  Help your children avoid the habit of checking their phone right before and after sleep.  Speak up about media concerns. When it seems no one else thinks it’s problematic or an emergency, then everyone goes along as if nothing is wrong, much like the experiment on smoke and peer pressure. Talk to schools, other parents, etc.  Other people have concerns, they just don’t realize that they’re not the only ones.

Title: Livingood daily
Author: Dr livingood
Notes: Would you trade your arms and legs for $15 million? Health is your biggest asset. People don’t plan on getting truly sick, but most do. Medicine was created for emergencies. Health care is not designed to make people healthy. How would you fix a pond full of sick fish? Clean up the water. The U.S. has terrible rates of death by disease and injury compared to similar countries. Its medical system is one of the leading causes of death and injury in the nation. We don’t have a “Healthcare system”, we have a sick-care system. Your health is up to you, no one will come for you. It is your responsibility. Programs are short-lived. Habits last, your way of life lasts. Health is like a formula. Health is all about function, not looks or just feelings. Usually, when you are at 60% of functioning and healing (or health) is when  you have your first symptom. So when you have symptoms, your health is way below what it seems. You don’t feel your kidney problems until 10% functioning usually. We can’t judge our health simply by how we feel. We can treat symptoms, or get to the cause. Start building health to get it. You are your greatest doctor. Your body heals itself, and is always running at 100% power. But you can’t get the power if there is interference. The three T’s of interference: Thoughts, toxins, traumas. Give your body good soil to grow in, removing interferences, and it will grow and flourish. Thoughts: gratitude (put things in perspective), take a break (mindful walk, be still, spend time in rest and digest state, get oxygen by breathing, , sleep). Fix your food. We idolize food, making everyday a “vacation” day. Start with 21 days of reset with food: cut sugar, eat more fat, eat clean protein,eat good nutrients, don’t eat too much or snack all the time. Most of our excess weight is sugar, not from fat.  Temporarily take a break from all sugars: flour and grains, sugar water, alcohol, fruit (except grannysmith apples, grapefruit, limes, lemons, and some berries),  tubers (potatoes, sweet potatoes, yams, minimize carrots), sweeteners and fake sweeteners. Use Stevie if needed. Do this for 21 days, just to break your sugar addiction, then add healthy sugar back in, like honey, fruit, whole grains, potatoes, etc. For fat, use olive oil, and cook with coconut, avocado, and grapeseed.  Avoid oil-roasted nuts. Avoid milk and dairy. Eat good fats like nuts and avocados, seeds, etc. Eat clean protein: pasture-raised chickens, moderate pork (well-fed, organic), organic grass-fed cows, wildcaught fish, avoid bottom feeders, eggs, no soy (#1 good food). Avoid corn. Focus on getting nutrients. Fuel the vehicle with nutrient dense snacks, like peppers, cucumbers, broccoli, other veggies, hummus, boiled eggs, avocados, raw nuts, granny Smith apples, coconut oil, greens, supergreen smoothies, etc. . Try fasting. Mult0le methods: smoothi smoothi dinner, or eat within a 6-hour window (intermittent fasting) like 12pm to 6pm, or rotational fasting (switch up the 6-h9ur window each day).

Title: Bad therapy
Author: Abigail shrier
Notes: Do the benefits outweigh the risks? They don’t always. Wanting to help is not the same as helping. Many therapists want to help. We as parents offload our responsibility. We also fell prey to having kids be our friends, people we never want to disappoint or inconvenience. How much does talking about bad, serious things, help us? Teens who don’t have a diagnosis feel left out. It is hard for them to have all their friends suffering. Most of Gen z believes they need mental health therapy. It is not just about social media or tech use. Psychologists have created terms for every struggle, endless disorders. More therapy has increased mental illness. More help should not create more issues. Psychologists mention three issues teens deal with that past gens didn’t: smart phones, covid, climate change. Psychologists don’t fight smart phones though. Schools let kids use devices as a pacifier, because “it keeps them calm”. They also didn’t speak against covid lockdowns. They support climate anxiety. Instead of calm our children, we “should adopt their anxiety”. They suggest that we don’t reassure our children, but instead bemoan ourselves and fear monger with our kids. Kids put lots of worries toward their parents just to see how they respond. Don’t validate every one of their fears.  But most young people’s concerns are not about. Climate change, etc. They are largely worried about social interaction, and how they fare in school, etc. Gen Z is largely typified by fear. They have an external locus of control. Therapy defines the individual as incapable of handling their issues, and outs them into the hands of an expert. The poor mental health means unparalleled profits for investors in business and tech businesses.  Therapists can treat kids by treating parents. Parents unwittingly impact their kids for better or worse. Treating the kid is one tiny part of the process, if it ends up working at all. But kids spend almost  all of their time with parents. If your kids therapist doesn’t tall about the terminating date of therapy on the first visit, there is a problem. They may treat them like an annuity, thinking they are healthy but opening them up just to be sure, to keep the money coming. Therapy can harm and does in many cases. How would a malevolent person teach someone to be sad? 1. Teach them to spend inordinate time thinking about their painful feelings.  Feelings are cued by many things. They are not always accurate, or interpreted correctly. We have to repress feelings sometimes.  Asking how someone feels is not a good thing to ask. It does not prompt them to think of happy things. Happiness is actually a rather rare feeling in the course of a day or week.  State of mind that make us more successful is action orientation, not state orientation. Focus on action or the goal, not current feelings or state. You can’t change the state. 2. Increase rumination. Make them think about their past a lot, about painful experiences. Being overly prone to talk about your pain is a symptom of depression. It is practicing depression. We also signal to kids that happiness is the goal. And the more we chase happiness, the more we are sad. It’s not cool to talk about your strengths, because it seems like privilege. Depression is socially rewarded. We tend to forget gratitude. 4. Affirm and validate kids worries.  Exposure therapy is one of the few evidences in cbt therapy.  We need practice sitting with discomfort. Help kids do things they are uncomfortable with.  Banishing normal chaos is the exact opposite of what we want to give our kids. Don’t remove inconveniences. Don’t make your life and your child’s life harder. Kids today are always observed. We tend to never give them privacy, they can’t spend time being responsible for themselves. More monitoring is bad, and equivalent to adding anxiety or stress. Monitoring has increased anxiety.  We need to learn to do things with the pain, with loss, without medication. Suicidality is a withdrawal symptom of antidepressants. Medicating a child is numbing them to life, when they need all of it for the building of their musculature for life.  Not everyone is helped by talking about their problems.  A dose of repression seems to be a good remedy in many instances. What often works is accepting responsibility, that only you can move on for you. Your biggest threat to your parent-child relationship is the therapist they are going to see.  10. Create treatment dependency. Hyperchondriacs create physical distress by worrying about physical distress or issues. It is self-fulfilling. The epicenter of bad therapy in your child’s life is likely your kid’s school.  Emotional checking are a state orientation. It’s like asking yourself how you feel after 2 minutes of hiking a mountain. You’ll never make it.many schools are legally not required, or able to avoid, parental informing about children’s mental health. They can give therapy and other services, gender affirming care, etc., behind parents’ backs. Whatever you focus on will grow. We are watering the weeds in our kids. Teachers are not trained or bound by ethical guidelines like therapists are many educators prompt trauma sharing in school. In the past, no matter what happened at home, kids could take refuge in the order at school when adults were mature and helpful. Now they find no refuge.what kids say earlier in school can be held on their record forever, and will follow them later in their life. Survival is built on implicit learning, just doing. We don’t need to monitor and have adult oversight for every kid’s implicit learning. There is no other way for them to learn it than to do it, while not being spied on or watched.  Our kids are taught to mindread their parents and spie on them for their school and self’s sake, making parents the enemy for the school counselor. Justifications for accommodations are often vague. Lowering expectations for perfectly capable students is hurtful. Violent  kids are “treated” unprofessional, not punished or disciplined, receiving no social consequences or authoritative consequences. Students exploit therapy to get out of their least favorite classes. Trauma studies have confounding variables issues, and selection is prone to bias, yet childhood trauma is used to justify public health decisions. True trauma is different from adversity. We are making everything “trauma”. We are teaching victimization or victimhood. Those from low backgrounds need high standards to rise to that goal, not low expectations. Those from less-than-ideal circumstances can rise to the occasion, and treating them that way is netter than otherwise. Treat kids as if they are resilient. The majority of people who suffered through 9-11 healthy emerged from it and continued with their life. We use “trauma” as a crutch or explanation for our troubles. It’s an easy answer to difficult problems. It’s a slippery argument with no proof, that we can blame our current issues on trauma.   Repressed memory: the predecessor to the body keeps the score.  Memories are not stored in body tissue. We hold memory Explicitly in mind, not implicitly in body. Elementary kids are not war vets. There is too muchbwe don’t know about the brain. We extrapolate too much about trauma, the brain, and problematic behavior or experiences.  Groups Haring may cause kids to remember things that never happened.   Trauma-loving therapists have pathologies mental health. By asking kids distressing questions, we plant in their minds the idea that their family might not be as loving as they thought, or that the world is worse than they thought, etc. We are , in a way, hurting them and their worldview. You could say we are traumatizing them in the way we currently use the word in popular  discourse. DARRE increased teen drug use. “Traumainformed care” encouraged people to about struggles, increasing pain. Hell is thinking about yourself.  Teaching empathy in school is problematic. We can only be empathetic towards one or a few people at a time, and we tend to be terrible to others. Trauma increases tattleing. Children tattleing rarely requires rule of law to believe. It becomes like stalin’s Russia or mao’s China.   Gen X decided they wanted their kids to like them for the sacrifices they made, to be their friends. Most young adults that cut off their parents just needed space and breath, because their parents didn’t give them space.  We shouldn’t tell our kids to not do things because it would rock our world or hurt us, we should tell them to make their own decisions, but tell them what we think is smart or not.  In America, we blame the parents when a child mouths off at their parent. In other countries, we blame the child.  Permissive parents create bad kids. Kids need authority to be healthy, to feel well. If they don’t find it from their parents at home, they look for it in other places, like extremist groups.  Don’t medicate your children.  Children are not weak unless we treat them that way. Don’t insist they are always children. Don’t give kids freedom t99 late, when they have passed the phase of wanting to enlarge their world and take on responsibility in that way. Don’t avoid your anxiety. Don’t avoid conflict with your kids. Kids know they are being patronized. We have taken decisions from our kids. We don’t give them independence. Treat kid’s anxiety with independence. They will gain confidence and a locus of control when they try and learn. Until recently, we let kids fail and learn in small ways. We let them run their own plays, endure moderate stress, etc.  We meet to let kids have a broader set of relationships. We need them to feel like they are part of a network. They need stable social webs. Don’t spoonfeed your children, teens, and young adults.  Raise your kids well, you’re the only one who can.

Title: Change your brain, change your life
Author: Daniel g amen
Notes: deep limbic system activity is correlated with negative emotion. Females generally have a larger deep limbic system than men: greater sense of smell, awareness of emotion, connection to others, negative emotion and sensitivity. Thoughts are real, in that they are electrical signals in your brain. They affect your physiology. Notice how negative thoughts effect your body. Your body reacts to every thought you have. Notice how positive thoughts effect your body. Notice how your body reacts to every thought you have. Think of bad thoughts as pollution. Understand that your automatic thoughts do not always tell the truth. You don’t have to believe every thought that goes through your head. Talk back to “ants”, the thoughts marching through your system. Exterminate the ants. Write them down, and talk back to them. Thoughts sometimes lie to you: always or never thinking, focusing on the negative or negativity bias in perception or memory, fortune telling (catastrophizing or predicting bad things), mindreading, thinking with your feelings or believing your feelings, guilt beating or shoulding, labeling (jerk, arrogant, etc.), personalizing (making events about you), blaming (victimhood). When you blame, you revoke your own personal power in the situation. Play the glad game from Pollyanna, find something to be glad about. Question things. Train yourself to recognize ants and remove them.  Spend time with people who believe in you, who support your progress, who help you feel good about yourself. Limbic bonding is one key to success of groups like AA. Limbic bonding between parent and child iskey to their avoidance of risky problematic behavior. Spend 1 on 1 time with your child. Keep it positive, and spend time with your child without teaching or lecturing. Do much more listening than talking.  Build people skills to help heal limbic bonds. Keep the relationship fresh, notice the good, take responsibility for keeping the relationship strong, never take it for granted, protect the relationship, assume the best about the other person, communicate clearly, maintain and protect trust, deal with difficulties and stick up for what you think is right, make time for each other.  Recognize the importance of physical touch.   Bonding is a two-way street. Lack of affection increases distance which increases lacking appearance of affection, etc., etc. Touch is essential to our humanity. Surround yourself with great smells.  Pleasing scents are anti-inflammatory to the limbic system. Build a library of wonderful memories. Depressed people have selective memories.  Early patterns predispose people to see certain patterns.  They live in a negative universe. Change brain chemistry by by remembering positive things by calling positive memories. By remembering the bad things, we continually filter. Remember the times in your life that were charged with positive emotion. Write them in detail, with your senses.  Make a list of the ten happiest times in your life. This disposes you to react in a positive way.  Try physical exercise. It increases endorphines that induce a sense of wellbeing. Many tech advances have eliminated physical exercise from our life. Exercises gives your more energy, normalizes mellotonin, makes you feel better. Find out what workout you like best. Get an aerobic exercise activity. Low fat Is not the answer. We need good fats. We need a balance of good fats carbs and proteins.    Dealing with basal  ganglia problems: kill the fortune telling ants (write down your thought, label the thought as fortune telling, talk back to the thought and let it go), use guided imagery (train relaxation, be alone, train your mind to be quiet, go and see in your mind somewhere you want to go, a safe haven), try diaphragmatic breathing (breath with your belly for a few minutes, meditate breathing deeply, place a book on your stomach to learn how to breath), try meditation (self hypnosis, flow or hypnotic state. Sit comfortably, pick a spot on the wall and count to 20 and close your eyes as you get to twenty, breath in peace and calmness, breath out tension, squeeze eye lids and let then slowly relax, relax your whole body the same, ride an escalator down counting to 20, enjoy how relaxed you feel, imagine how you want to be rather than how you are, imagine your safe haven), think about the 18-40-60 rule (when you are 60, you won’t care what others think, focus on what you want to do with life), learn how to deal with conflict (we teach others how to treat us by what we refuse or accept from them, by what we tolerate, we teach them what is ok by avoiding or giving in to conflict. Be assertive, don’t give in to others’ anger or opinions, say what you mean and believe, maintain self control, be kind, be firm in your stance), consider medications, watch your nutrition (keep diet steady and balanced, b vitamins, chamomile, eliminate caffeine).  The capacity to generate goals and achieve them is an evolved function of the pfc, not a socially constructed artifact.  The pfc helps you feel or recognize feelings. Thoughtfulness and impulse control are the pfc.  Underachieving pfc cannot appropriately inhibit the limbic system. Pfc issues increase chances of short attention span, distractability, impulse control issues, hyperactivity, lateness, disorganization, procrastination, unavailability of emotions, lack of perseverance, poor time management, mis perceptions, poor judgment, trouble learning from experience, social anxiety, short-term memory problems.  People with pfc issues often regret things they do, have problems with attention span, and have problems expressing themselves. Social anxiety may be a hallmark of pfc problems.  They have trouble activitating this part of the brain under stress. Social situations require concentration and dealing with uncertainty. Pfc deactivation often causes a person to go blank in conversation causing discomfort.   People with add need extra excitement to kick in their pfc function. The pfc sends inhibitory signals to other parts of the brain. When underactive, it fails to help control other parts of the brain.  Many people with add unconsciously seek conflict to stimulate their pfc. They don’t plan to, and deny it, but they do it. The heightened conflict helps them feel more tuned in.  Worrying increases stress chemicals that keep the brain active. Reactions from others keep them stimulated, or simply being upset increases stimulation. People with add may grind people to pick on, or become the class clowns. Many people with add have “filing cabinets” that only they understand, they are disorganized, chronically late, etc. Many people with add are moody or negative. if they can’t find turmoil with others, they seek it within themselves.   Schizophrenia: distortion of reality from fiction.   Because of poor pfc  activity, they are unable to process their issues, pain, etc., and can develop delusions to explain it. Psychotic disorders often have decreased pfc activity.  Pfc is especially susceptible to injury from head injury, even when there is no loss of consciousness, etc. Your brain is very soft, the skull is very sharp. Minor blows to head can alter character.  Getting hit by football in the head.    Fogginess, excessive daydreaming, tendency to make repetitive mistakes, lack of empathy for others, etc., can be related to pfc issues.  Pfc prescriptions: goal setting (1-page miracle. Clearly write out your main goals on a page, write subheadings, write what you want not what you want. Make it personal, update it frequently, put it somewhere you can see it everyday), focus on what you like a lot more than what you don't like (like giving attention to others for what we love about them, rather than what we dislike, we should focus and give attention to what we love in our life and about ourselves. Don’t reinforce the negative behavior, reward and reinforce the positive), have meaning purpose and excitement in your life (people with ADD need more of this to excel), get organized (get help when you need it, don’t be embarrassed to ask for help, set clear goals in each area of your life, devote some time to organizing your workspace, break down tasks, do unpleasant tasks first to save fun for last, ), consider brainwave biofeedback (most children have too little beta brainwaves (rest) and too much theta brainwaves (daydreaming), learning to take control.  Have something to remind you of the positive in your life, of what you want to reward yourself for, to reinforce, to care about. Let the negative go, focus on what you want more of.  Try audio/visual stimulation techniques (more research needed). Don’t be someone else's stimulant. Be less reactive, deny them the adrenaline rush of conflict, etc. Use humor but not sarcasm.   Consider stimulant medication.  Watch your pfc nutrition: eliminate simple sugars and carbohydrates, stick with fats, proteins, and complex carbs. Try Mozart to reduce theta brainwaves. Cingulate system: moving from idea to idea, flexibility, learning a new system of things, cooperation, planning and setting future goals, seeing options. Problems: worry or getting stuck on things, ocd, rumination, a reset button always pressed, rigidity, holding on to hurts from the past, the need to “do it now”, only eating certain foods. “No” seems to be the favorite word for those with  Cingulate problems.  Ocd is compulsions.  Ocd-spectrum disorders (addictive, ticks, eating disorders, gambling, compulsive shopping).  Holding grudges.   Many of these people who have cingulate issues have parents or family who also do. It becomes a multigenerational. Rigid parents also apparently produce some of these results. Give a child a choice, so that they don't have to revolt and say no to something they feel forced to do.  Cingulate system prescriptions: notice when you’re stuck, distract yourself, and come back to the problem later.  Think through answers before automatically saying “no”, take a deep breath and think.  Write out options and solutions when you are stuck, a list of things you can do about it and what you can’t. Seek counsel from others when you feel stuck (reality checks, counsel, help).  Memorize and recite the serenity prayer when bothered by repetitive thoughts. Take a break from an argument, distract yourself, and come back to it later (use the bathroom as an excuse, read for a minute to distract yourself).  Try making paradoxical requests (ask for the opposite, or say “you probably wouldn’t want … would you?”). Oppositional children: let child know that their oppositional behavior  will not get them anything positive, that you won’t be bullied as a parent, and then distract the child from their fears or the thought that got stuck. Authoritative parents are most successfully.  Rule 1: no arguing with parents, you must comply the first time. Don’t get emotional. Do it quickly.  Rule 2: no arguing with parents: draw the line between sharing opinion and arguing. Tell your child “ we want to hear your opinion”, but arguing means you’ve made your point more than two times.  This works within the context of a good parent-child relationship, where you spend time with and bond with your child. Exercise. During exercise, you raise serotonin levels.  Temporal lobe prescriptions: 1. Create a library of wonderful experiences, 2. Sing whenever wherever you can, 3. Use humming and toning to tune up your brain (toning: elongated vowel sounds for a prolonged period of time, such as ah ee eh o oo mm), 4. Listen to classical music (Mozart, complex music, soothing music, rather than simple and repetitive music), 5. Learn to play a musical instrument, 6. Move in rhythms (chanting, dancing, body movement, moving in rhythm), 7. Consider temporal lobe meds if necessary, 8. Get enough sleep, 9. Eliminate caffeine and nicotine, 10. Watch your nutrition (avoid sugar, etc. Eat balanced). Drug users likely use drugs to self-medicate issues in their brain.   Drugs deteriorate the brain. Caffeine decreases brain stimulation and activity. Drugs alter the barrier to violence we have in our brain, either raising or lowering the threshold where we resort to violence. Relational prescriptions for self: spend time together, smells good, build positive memories, touch each other, kill the ANTs (automatic negative thoughts), predict good things, take deep breaths, deal with conflict, focus on what you want and post it in a place you see it, focus on what you like about your partner, new ways to positively stimulate the relationship, learn to say i’m sorry, think before you say or do, notice bad thinking patterns, stop nagging, exercise together, have a carb snack if you are angry or such, use notes to remind your partner you care, move together in rhythm, remember good times, protein snacks. Relational prescriptions for partner: don’t let partner isolate themselves, help them around the house, gentle physical support, take care of yourself, help them look at positive side, pace breathing to help them mirror it, do not be your partner’s riddled (stimulant), help partner with organization, take a break when they are angry, take anger seriously when they are angry. Seek help when self-help has not worked. If the software hasn’t worked, change the hardware. Depression is contagious, causing others anxiety or to see things negatively. Depression is not absence of feeling, but presence of painful feelings. There is a stigma for getting help, but successful people are those that seek help. How to help others get help: plant seeds sparingly (talk about getting help sometimes), share books or articles. Save money to find the best physician you can, someone who has seen thousands of cases like yours, specialists, seek advice from medical support groups, check credentials, set up an interview to get to know them, read their writings or hear them speak, look for respect and caring. Don't settle for an average generalist. When our brains work right, we are really who we really are, and more able to become who we really want to be, more able to imagine a healthy God, more able to choose well, more loving, more beneficial to society. The brain does not exist in a vacuum, but all behavior starts in the physical functioning of the brain.

Title: The 7 habits of highly effective people
Author: Stephen r. covey
Notes: Character ethics, not personality ethics. There are laws that cannot be broken, only fought against. Personality ethics is trying to take a short-cut. But can you really shortcut life, like skipping years of piano or sports practice? We have paradigms or ways that we see the world, maps of the territory. A map ≠ territory, it just represents or interprets parts of it. How we see the world impacts what we do. We are conditioned to see in specific ways, and thus have differing perspectives when seeing the same facts. By changing our paradigms, living by the principles of life - or valuing true principles, we can change much quicker than otherwise, and truly change instead of masking growth in a world of similar fakes. Who we are shines brighter than how we communicate, etc. We cannot escape showing our true character, thus why we trust some people even with their clumsy skills in speaking, etc. Life is, by nature, highly interdependent. Those who can’t choose interdependence well often are fleeing from internal dependencies, such as letting others’ weaknesses ruin our emotional lives, or feeling victimized by things out of our control. Thus people abandon marriages, children, and many other social responsibilities in the name of “liberation”, “living their truth”, “asserting themselves”, “authenticity”.  Interdependence is a far more mature advanced life, where you are self-reliant and capable, but also realize that far more is accomplished when we work together.  You derive a great sense of worth from within, but also recognize the need for love, giving, and receiving love. You realize you need the best thinking of others to join your own. Being interdependent, youcan share yourself deeply and meaningfully, and have access to others’ potential and resources. Interdependence is a choice only independent people can make. Dependent people don’t own enough of themselves. Private victories precede public victories. Habits 1, 2, and 3 move a person from dependence to independence. 4, 5, and 6 are built upon this base, to work on public victories in the world of interdependence. Effectiveness is both the golden eggs and the goose that laid them. Effectiveness = production, and production capability. We look for shortcut returns, we often lose our production capacity. We stop taking care of the lawn mower, or spend the money that earns us interest, or stop developing ourselves. We must continually improve our own production capacity, to avoid being dependent or locked into situations. When we focus on outcomes rather than preserving the underlying relationship, we can become impatient, neglectful, controlling, logically faulty and justifying. The love, richness, spontaneity, and commitment of real relationships is a product of our prior investment in the production capacity, the relationship. Don’t kill the goose, or poison or let it become malnourished.  Don’t leave others in an organization with “dying geese” physical assets that you didn’t upkeep. many times, others are our production capacity for the things we desire, because only together can we accomplish the goal.  You can buy a person’s hand or back, but you can’t truly buy their heart or brain. You can buy agreements and labor, but not relationship and ingenuity. Employees, customers, family, friends, are all volunteers offering their best parts: their heart and mind, and they can choose to withdraw or offer them somewhere else. So much focus on the golden egg kills the goose. That short-term bottom line isn’t all-importan0t. Effectiveness lies in balance. Focusing only on PC or the goose is like spending a life doing nothing but running only to brag about running, or being an eternal student that never produces any eggs. Read as if, in the next 48 hours, you will teach someone what you read. As you live these principles, you will care less about what others think of you, and more about what others think of themselves and their worlds, including their relationship with you. Your emotional life will no longer be built on others’ weaknesses. “That which we obtain too easily, we esteem too lightly…heaven knows how to put a proper price on its goods”. Between the stimulus and response, man has the freedom to choose. As humans, we have imagination, conscience, and independent will. We are self-aware. Like Victor frankl, we can choose how we respond even when all other choices are taken away. We are not determined. We study animals and ill people to decipher human behavior, but these do not represent the territory of man’s  experience/capability. If we do not account for how we see ourselves and others, our awareness, we are unable to understand how others perceive and feel about themselves and the world, and we project ourselves on others while thinking we are objective reality. Our behavior is a function of our decisions, not our conditions. Response-ability, the ability to choose your response = responsibility, not reactivity.  Responsible people are value driven, they choose based on their values.  To be reactive is to empower others’ weaknesses to control your feelings, thoughts, behaviors.  Until you say “I am what I am today because of the choices I made yesterday”, you cannot say “I choose otherwise”. It’s not what happens, it’s our response. Our basic nature is to act, not be acted upon. Good habits depend upon your proactive muscles. Use your resourcefulness and initiative. Many people wait for others to help them. Create an atmosphere where people can seize opportunities and solve problems in an increasingly self-reliant way. If you wait, you will be acted upon.  Act, or be acted upon. To be proactive is to face reality, and then choose to respond for the better. It’s not positive thinking, it’s choosing positive responses.  We can see how we think about our power by our language. Do we use reactive or proactive language? We have a circle of influence and a circle of concern. Focusing on the circle of influence makes it grow, and vice versa.  For everything, we either have direct control, indirect control, or no control.  We solve direct control problems by working on habits. We solve indirect control problems by changing our methods of influence. We solve “no control” problems by learning to peacefully accept and live with them.  These three proactive approaches are all within and expand our circle of influence. Focus on what you choose to be, not what you have or do not have. Like Joseph in Egypt, you may be unjustly imprisoned, but you can always choose what you want to be and how to use your influence. Choose your own weather, by accepting the things you can’t control, and focusing effort on things you can.  We choose actions, not consequences. Picking up a stick with consequences you don’t want is a past mistake, and is in your circle of concern, not influence. acknowledge and learn from the mistake immediately. It is not others or our mistakes that hurt us, but our response to them. As we make and keep commitments, we establish an inner integrity, awareness of self-control, and courage and strength to accept more responsibility. Little by little, our honor becomes greater than our mood, because we keep our promises to ourselves.

Title: The book you wish your parents had read
Author: Philippa perry
Notes:
High bursts of emotion at your child’s behavior is a signal that you are reacting to a past memory, to your experience as a child, not theirs. Think when this happens, “am I really reacting to this event in the present? Or something long ago?” look back at yourself when young with compassion. If you find yourself longing for a break from your children all the time, perhaps you need to give your younger self a break, more care, etc. Try revealing your inner critic: Write down your negative thoughts, do they remind you of anyone else? Drop “good” and “bad”. Stop judging and labeling. Describe what you see and appreciate, and praise effort. Praise what you want to see more of, comment on what you do right. Suspend judgment, and hold opinions loosely, as they it will all likely change. We make dirt for our kids, an environment, the soil, and let them thrive in it. Divorced parents need to have contact with each parent, and for their parents to communicate civilly. Admit rather than denying resentment if it exists. Then try to change. Life will change as you have a family, it will be difficult. Arguing: context, feelings. Styles of bad arguing: tennis attacks, squirrel distraction, becoming a martyr sacrifice to keep the peace. Ideally, work with one issue at a time and deal with what the issue is really about. The ideal argument is about understanding. Do it with I statements, and curiosity. Play the role of a mediator in family arguments. Think in terms of how each feels. Acknowledge feelings. Embrace your vulnerability. Don’t assume the intent of the other person. Is your relationship based on anxiety? Or is your partner your friend? Someone you feel calm with usually? Respond to your partner’s bids for connection/intimacy. Look for the good. Seek and ye shall find. Find things to appreciate. Turn towards bids, not away. Feelings: responsiveness to children/baby’s feelings teach them to interact with and hear their feelings, that they are not to be avoidedand will pass eventually.  Don’t disallow feelings, because you want your child to be happy. Don’t be in denial, that makes your child’s feelings more problematic because they are not letting them at as signals, and they learn to ignore their feelings, to stuff them down.  Encourage your child to draw, etc., how they feel. Help them be heard each day, to truly be seen.  When feelings are validated, they no longer need to prove their point. Talk about feelings rather than pushing them away. Feel with, don’t deal with. When children are felt with, they don’t need to feel it anymore. By validating the feelings, connections are made, empathy is practiced, soothing occurs.  By telling your child they are being silly, they won’t tell you anything remotely silly again. They can’t differentiate between issues and simple feelings. Closing off the channels of communication closes you off to warning signs, especially dangerous in terms of mental health, abuse, etc. That you would want to know about. The demand that we be happy undermines our lives.  We are often wrong about what will satisfy us. Turn down pain and sadness, and you turn down all feelings. Happiness is about relationships. Validating feelings strengthens bonding between parent and child. Distracting from emotions is a trick and manipulation. It’s a deceptive tactic and hurts trust and relationships. Help your kids with frustration rather than distracting them. If you constantly distract them, you are hurting their habits of concentration and focus. Be with the child and acknowledge their feelings. Tell the truth, and help them with empathy, rather than avoidance (negotiate: what are their concerns really?). Treat your  child as a person, feel with them, don’they deal with them.  Be wary of rules and advice about pregnancy. Your pregnancy and child are not projects. Your child is a lifelong relationship that will develop.rules can also give us a false sense of control. Pregnancy and childbearing are by nature a risk and cary uncertainty.  Don’t catastrophize. The story you tell yourself is the story you tell your child. Choose optimism. When pregnant and aware of the fetus’ sex, we unconsciously label and categorize or stereotype their behavior, even before born. Be wary of predertermining your child’s characteristics, and care about how you perceive your child as a fetus (are they a burden, or a joy). Feelings are feelings, never right or wrong. Be honest about how you are feeling toward your child, and acknowledge it so you can move forward accordingly. What stories are you telling yourself? Your birth will not live up to an ideal. Steer in the direction you want, and meet what comes. Debrief from the birth experience as much as you need to. Babies naturally know the “breast crawl” (finding the nipple). Skin on skin contact is important for babies. New parents need to be heard and listened to, to know that their experience is normal, that they are not monsters for their weaknesses, and that they are understood and accepted. They need this radical acceptance in order to be able to give it to their child. Not feeling for yourself impairs your ability to feel for your children. It’s not the ruptures that count, but how they are repaired, how relationships are reformed. Life will be easier for a baby if they first feel they belong, that the world is a safe place. Babies are preformed to form attachments. Foster a secure attachment style. Avoidant: you learned that others are untrustworthy and can’t be relied upon, so you stop asking for their help or reaching out. Insecure: you learned that you need to make a lot of noise to be noticed, and will probably get ignored, and can’t take companionship for granted, cause people make leave you. Dismissive: you learned that others will ask you to meet their needs, will abuse you, etc.  Babies give coercive cries, and it’s best to respond to them, so the baby knows they are safe and develops a sense of wellbeing in the world. Loneliness warns us to do something. It feels hard to tackle, because fixing it feels threatening in social situations. But try to tackle isolation and loneliness as quickly as possible. Watch out for feelings of superiority/inferiority and choose to join social groups anyway.  Trust your child to separate at their own pace. Train your child by being responsive, but increasing the time and space between their cry and coming to their aid. What matters is the relationship. It isn’t the mistake that matters, as much as it is mending it. Let your child take the lead, helping them do things for themselves, and not rescuing them. Children need a safe place to play so they are not distracted by being told “no” all the time.  Children do not need more than a few basic toys. More toys is not better. Children need free play, time to use their imagination. Help your child start their play and then back off when they are content. Age-mixed play is different from play with peers their same age, the lessons and learning are unique and helpful. Tell your child you have confidence in their ability to find something to do when they are bored. All behavior is communication. Your child will imitate your behavior. Your behavior is co-created. For young children, behavior is the only way they can communicate. The concepts of “good” and “bad” are unhelpful. Behavior is convenient or inconvenient. What is their behavior trying to say? How is their behavior co-created with yours? Behind behavior, you find feelings. Put the feelings into words. Think of the situation from the child’s perspective. If you impose your will on your child, how will you like it when they learn to impose their will on others? It’s not about winning and losing. Go with what is working in the present, rather than what you fantasize about in the future. We say, “what if…”?” And catastrophize. If what is working stops working, then make a change.  Abilities to behave well: tolerating frustration, flexibility, problem solving, seeing and feeling things from others’ points of view. Children may learn these skills at different times and stages of their life. Sometimes, children want your attention and love so much they will seek negative attention as a final attempt rather than getting no attention. If we manipulate children, we cannot be upset if they manipulate us or others. Tech by example. Bribes should be the exception, not the norm. Play is “work” for children. To teach kids the value of money, we must teach them the value of people. Rather than forcing your child to insincerity do things, teach them by example, make sure others feel well-treated by doing things yourself. Invest time positively earlier, rather than negatively later. Try writing down your child’s point of view when you find it difficult to understand or deal with. Help behavior by putting feelings into words. Naming the pain of your child will not make it worse. The “they’re tired” excuse parents make for a child’s behavior is overused, as is the “they just need attention”. Children are feeling their feelings. Thinking they are just tired is even more infuriating for the child. Many institutionalized behaviors are treatable early on by changing habits.when working through issues, collaborate with your child, brainstorm solutions, and give your child the lead. Don't be the clever one with all the answers. Have the patience to wait for your child to think, and let them develop. Children do not have tantrums because they want to. They are feeling their feelings. See ghe child from their point of view and stay calm. No one was ever healed by being shamed or feeling silly. Retaliation is punishing your child for having feelin reflect, don’t react. Young children cannot take in complex reasons. Whingeing : crying or whining. Their crying may remind you of your pain, and therefore you may subconsciously silence it and have a low tolerance for your child’s difficult feelings. Don’t lie to your children, even by omission. They will sense the atmosphere and come to their own conclusions if you don’t tell them the truth. There is an age-appropriate way to tell your child anything, so don’t withhold information that they have a right to know. Children will lie at some point, and we all do it at some point. Children witness their parents lying all the time. There is no reason that they should not lie if they see you do it. Often, children tell lies to deal with difficult parents who cannot remain calm, or to create a narrative for their feelings they don’t understand. The more we put our feelings into words, the less our children will need to lie to deal with feelings.  Don’Don’ overreact to what your child does or tells you, or they will keep it from you. They may want to keep some things for themselves. The goal is to be a safe person whom they can tell anything they wish to, so that true troubles don’t go unheard or unsaid/untreated/unhandled. If you irrationally punish your child and are more punitive, they are more likely to continue bad behavior and learn to lie.  Make a habit of being honest about your feelings and reasons for boundaries. Don’t make up reasons for family rules or other boundaries, or try to hide your feelings or lie about them. Be flexible and willing to see every child as an individual. Define yourself (your own feelings). Reason wars are “fact tennis”, and they don’t work because everyone has a different experience and need to be taken seriously from their point of view. When you are more considerate of your child, they become more considerate of you.  Define the problem, find the feelings behind the problem, brainstorm solutions. Keep naming your own feelings, because they really are the reason you do what you do and put down boundaries. Make the first move to repair the rupture. Update your expectations about their willingness to welcome your advice, etc. Help kids get the help they need, don’don’ label people as bad. The “bad lot” of kids you blame are someone else’s kid who is trying their best.  Teenagers are more likely to collaborate with you and be helpful if they feel like you are part of your life, that you spend time together and are in the same realm. How your child feels 
about and and sees themself will always , to some extent, be influenced by how you respond to them, how you delight in them, how you greet them, how you accept them. It is never too late to try to repair a rupture.

Title: The go-giver
Author: Bob burg, John David mann
Notes: The world is not a dog eat dog place. Test these principles by applying them in your life. People treat you largely as you expect them to treat you. Don’t waste your time. Law of value: give away more value than you are paid. Profitable things will happen. Your true work is determined by how much more you give in value than receive in payment. Give because you love to. This determines your value, your potential. The law of compensation determines how much you get paid. Law of compensation: your income is determined by how many people you serve, and how well you serve them. Your compensation is proportional to how many lives you touch. Anyone can succeed because anyone can give.  There are no limitations on what you can earn, because you can always serve more people. What you focus on is what you get. You can be good and wealthy. Sometimes you feel foolish, look foolish, but you do the thing anyway. Survive, save, and serve: three motives to earn money. Service is the most fulfilling. Do it like you love it. your network is the people who are invested in your success. The law of influence: watch out for the other guy. Your influence is determined by how abundantly you place other people’s interests first. No win-win (tit for  tat), or you owe me attitude. Focus on helping the other guy win. Give. What makes people attractive? They give. Givers are attractive. “You owe me” is you being a creditor, not a friend. Stop keeping score. Care more about their happiness than your own (this is success). The law of authenticity: you are your most valuable commodity. The most valuable gift you have to offer is yourself. 90% people skills. As long as you are trying to be someone else, you have no chance. Be a person (this is people skills, authenticity). The law of receptivity: it’s not better to give than receive, it’s insane to not receive. Every giving can happen only because it is also a receiving. Choose to receive. Don’t refuse the gifts of others. Be open to receive, welcoming. It is more “blessed” to give, but not more important or better. Plenty of people are nice, but don’t succeed. By giving, it is meant being a giving person, giving value to others. Add value to others’ lives. Value comes first, the money you receive comes as a natural result.  Money is not a measure of your goodness, but of your impact.

Title: The comfort crisis
Author: Michael easter
Notes: Rule 1: make it really hard. Rule 2: don’t die. Constant comfort is a radically new experience for humans. We are swimming in comfort. We experience 1st world stress, whereas our ancestors experienced life-or-death discomfort. We are less likely to die, but less healthy. Humans see gray, based on all the inputs we have perceived before. As we experience fewer problems, we lower our threshold for what we see as problems. We become less and less satisfied with what we now see. We are terrible at noticing this. Humans used to live wild, hunt, be close to the plants and animals they ate. Most of us have no idea what’s out on the edge of our potential. Misogi: What are you mentally and spiritually willing to put yourself through to become a better human? There should be a 50/50 chance of success. Fail half the time, or it’s not difficult enough. Failure 100 years ago meant you might die. But we vastly overestimate failure today, and underestimate the benefits. There’s adventure in the hero’s journey, struggling, internal locus, and using the tools you have. Native peoples have long held traditions of rites of passage rituals. 3 key stages: separation (venturing alone), transition (challenging battle/task), incorporation (reintegrating as a matured human). Rites of passage are largely gone from our modern world. There exists in all of us an archetypal need to be initiated. Misogi is a challenge that’s you against you. It’s not about comparison. Therefore, don’t post or share online, etc. about misogis. Some degree of challenge in life, that is not overwhelming, leads to increased resilience. Newness slows down our sense of time. This is why our childhood seemed slow. Everything was new to us. Getting outside of our comfort zone slows time, makes us aware of details. Most people say they would like to live in the country, but that’s least best for survival. Why would we want to live in open spaces? We are built for tribes of about no more than  150 people. The higher the density  of the population, the lower chance of happiness. Rediscover boredom, preferably outside, for minutes, hours, days. Boredom is a desire for desire, it’s a motivational state. Time in unfocused mode is critical. Resting is an effort. Constant attention can overwork our brain, it can be overdone. Wandering mind is necessary. Boredom helps you rest and reset. Constant focus and attention is like feeding our minds junkfood. Digital devices are a large part of our problem with unbroken distraction.  Your attention is the goal of these digital lab experiments.  We have slot machines in our pockets. We should learn to deal with boredom. Boredom increases creativity, by teaching you to think about doing things, to teach you to think on a different wavelength. Dealing with boredom is creativity. We are facing a creativity crisis. Steve Jobs believed in boredom, and didn’t let his own kids use the iPad. Instead of “less phone”, think “more boredom”. Given the choice, humans choose something they can control or predict. We evolved to look to the future and track information to help us survive. Nature is a necessary connection in our life for thriving. “Nature bathing”, or spending time immersed in nature, helps us heal in each area of our being. Biophilia is increasingly considered seriously as an antidote to our being stressed and overworked. Passing through nature is as easy as passing through the park on the way to work. Stop thinking of nature as “out there” somewhere else. Nature is a plant, your backyard, the lawn, park, hills, trees, etc. Spend time in all types of nature, especially wild nature. The wilder the nature, the better.  3 days in the wild is like a meditation retreat, the 3 day effect is notable in performance afterwards and continues.  We struggle with sleep, partly because we never spend enough time in adequate darkness and silence, and don’t physically exert ourselves enough.  We tend to decrease our senses in many areas (wearing shoes, etc.), but we increase our stimulus in hearing. We are in constant noise, and find “silence” uncomfortable. Silence-induced discomfort is a new learned behavior. More noise increases stress and anxiety. Even in anechoic chambers, we hear sound, because we make sound. There is sound everywhere, but we have increasingly drowned out the natural sounds of our world with loud noise, and are less aware of the sound that would otherwise be noticeable. Anechoic chambers and natural silence help us recalibrate to “silence” and lower our blood pressure and stress.  At h9ke silence is more relaxing than listening to Mozart, etc. Natural silence is better for us than most of the “relaxing” solutions we are sold. There are people in America with food insecurity, but the larger problem for most seems to be eating too much, or as the Japanese call it, “lonely mouth” or eating because you can and there I ls food. Most people could lose wight as well, but don’t because of the discomfort. Most on a “diet” stop after 5 weeks, because that is the average time when people feel the most discomfort, when their biology is telling them to get back to comfort to stay alive. We eat when we need reward hunger, a psychological reward for eating, more sonwhen we are stressed.  Early humans had few ways to store food, so they stored it in fat.  Real hunger drives just 25% of eating. Ask yourself “why are you eating?” Rather than if you are eating something specific at a specific time. Many people don’t know how to deal with stress. People who stay physically healthy simply choose a walk over ice cream, etc.  We have a lot more chronic stress than acute stress. We use ultraprocessed food as a cheep self-medication, to deal with the low-level chronic stress of day-to-day.  Stress eating is the reason most fad diets don’t work. Binging on a good diet doesn’t help. Keep track of what you eat, so you are accountable, watch yourself so you feel accountable. Eat unprocessed whole grains and tubers, fruits and vegetables, and low-ish fat animal protein. Unprocessed grains must be cooked in water to become edible (rice, quinoa, oatmeal).  Don’t eat into Supreme comfort each meal.  We no longer have the stress of lean times, of going without food.  We don’t gain weight in small consistent gains, but we also don’t gain it in big bursts. We tend to gain weight at particular important times in our life with stress (getting married, moving, holidays, etc.).  Our ancestors didn’t snack around the clock.  Lean times are a necessary part of optimizing health. When we burn tissue, we burn old tissue, like cancer, etc. The old cells in our body are related to lots of diseases.   Autophagy is natural at night during sleep. If you eat before bed, you don’t let your body take out the trash during sleep. For our ancestors, food was likely consumed during daylight hours, leaving long periods of fasting during the night. Hunger can be better than many things we try. Breakfast is not the most important meal. Embrace the discomfort of hunger. Think about your death everyday. The easier our lives get, the more uncomfortable we seem to become with death.  We act as if life is a checklist, a list of things to accomplish. The checklist is never-ending. This is the same reason we struggle with materialism. Mindfulness is the answer to this issue. Everyone is dying right now. To ignore this, is ignorance. Be Mindful of your death, that you are walking toward http://it.to think of death is the necessary tool for preparing for your deathbed. Greed, anger, and ignorance are the three main delusions. When our mind is not cared for, these delusions come up. Impermanence = nothing lasts, and therefore nothing can be held onto. All things pass away, all dies. Our false sense of permanence is the reason we put off doing the things we want to do.  People who think about their death are kinder and more charitable to both themselves and others. Thinking about death increases gratitude, thinking of what might not be, and what therefore is. Life is a privilege. Think of death in the morning, mid-day, and evening. Nature is cruel. The hunter often gives an animal a fast and painless death.  Carry the load. Non-western/non-industrialized peoples get lots of exercise, and burn more calories doing that exercise than industrialized peoples do. Many people in our society do hardly any exercise at all. Hunting and foraging is not just a physical exercise, but mental work. In the wild, we don’t lift perfectly measured weights, use padded weight machines, bulk up, or watch TV. The decisions and perseverance and mental aptitude necessary in real life, outdoor exercise is what keeps our minds sharp. Uneven ground forces us to burn more calories, to do more work.  Humans were made for carrying.  Carrying was likely more common than running. Most of us almost never carry anything difficult. It’s different than a marathon or a backpack or a weight room. Rucksack. Ruck is a verb, for those with rucksacks. Like the military, you always carry weight. 50 pounds is the most weight a soldier can thrive with. Rucking is strength and aerobics 101. Doing hard things makes the rest of life satisfying.sedentary jobs lead to shorter lives. Movement is perhaps the only “miracle cure”.  There is no such thing as too much exercise. Exercise can be more effective than medication, for things such as diabetes prevention. There is such thing as runner’runner’ knee. That’s why rucking is so good. We evolved to work this way. Mom takes 10 pounds, I take 50. We both go the same speed, and we socialize while doing so. Normal human exercise shouldn’t give you anxiety. It should feel normal to hike, walk, climb, carry, etc.  97% of our non-specific backpain is a result of our lifestyle, our captivity from modern life. We now do repitive odd movements, or are largely inactive and don’g do what we used to do.for example, sitting used to be done without chair backs, etc. Most of the leisure that our ancestors did involved using more muscles than we now use when sitting, sleeping, etc. We now become slaves to our laptops, and then blast our exercise in one hour. Better to do general body movements throughout the day. strong core and gluten are one of the best ways to prevent back pain. Squat, lunge, plank, hinge, carry, hang, etc. Carry things. Rucking helps people prevent low back pain. Carrying forces a person to stand tall and lock down the muscles that protect the spine. Our microbiome is in a way another organ in our body.  Our oversanitized life may keep us from developing our immunity, and make us more disease prone. We become more so one with our environment when we take it in fully. Food allergies disproportionately afflict those in developed nations.  Dirt is good. Diverse diet is good. Unprocessed plants, many of them raw. Don’t take antibiotics unless absolutely necessary.  Frequent bathing may prevent the immune system from adequately doing its job.  Japanese women who dive in the cold sea for sea creatures had better health, not worse. We need to burn energy through cold and hot weather. We tend to not do this. New events slow time. Fill your “scrapbook” with new experiences, contemplating your walk toward death.

Title: The age of magical overthinking
Author: Amanda montell
Notes: Halo effect: we see one attractive trait as evidence for the existence of others that we haven’t observed. Natural selection favored a paranoid mindset. Proportionality bias: We look for perfect ratios, we look for explanations. The greater the effect, the greater we desire the cause to be. Social media influencers foster reliance, instead of teaching you to think for yourself. Frequency bias, confirmation bias, and proportionality bias, create manifestation and law of attraction thinking. Frequency bias can lead to over-diagnosis simply because we heard about a condition recently. A toxic relationship is just a cult of one. Let those in a cult relationship know that if they ever want to get out, even just chat, you will be there (you won’t judge, interrogate, shame, etc.). They may not talk to you for a while, but they won’t forget. Sometimes it needs to be said so that they know that others see them suffering, and it’s not too late to cut their losses. Sunk cost fallacy: We evolved to avoid defeat at all costs. When we find ourselves in a losing situation, we tend to persevere, telling ourselves it will work out. We don’t want to be seen as having made a poor choice. In nature, we use the sunk cost fallacy to cast ourselves in a socially positive light. We don’t want to admit we made a bad bet. Honoring sunk costs may make us seem more consistent, like we know ourselves well, and can be trusted. To appear socially valuable, we feel pressure to appear the best we can. We want to believe the fairytale version of us as much as we want to share it with others. We have a bias toward additive solutions. We rarely think to take something away. We are biased toward adding new things to solve problems, and forget that maybe we don’t need what we have, and removing this may solve the problem. We have a capacity for attention, and the amount of information we are exposed to exceeds that capacity. Zero-sum fallacy: the false assumption that another party’s gain means your loss. Whenever someone profits from exchange, we assume the other person was ripped off, yet that is not true. People rarely pay for something they don’t value as much as they spend on it.
