Some things, as in the past, are zero-sum, like how much pizza you can each get from one pie. Yet, win-win scenarios are the entire reason we accomplish more in groups. Our monetary system has made this extremely abstract, so we find it more difficult to decide value measurements. It is also difficult to tell who is in our social circle, and who we deem our competitors. Our “worst competitors” usually remind us of ourselves. They may be the people we may click with best. In the eastern world, places like Japan, people are more likely to be happy playing a small role in a prestigious company. They are fine being a small fish in a big pond.  Social media inflates social comparison, and imposter syndrome. We don’t know who to compare ourselves to, so we compare against everyone's fairytale life. These people are also likely great collaborators, but we think their wins mean our loss.  Women tend to compare themselves with their “superiors”, and men with their “inferiors”. Girls therefore learn in middle school to see the “threats” around them. Capitalism + feminism is classic zero-sum bias fuel. Women “collaborate” with other women only to tear them down later. Tokenizing members of marginalized communities promotes a culture of noxious infighting. To adopt tokenism, you have to sell your community out: instead of blaming institutions and systems around you for your problems, you end up blaming your community. We spend time frustrated with those we think of as “in our circle” in some way. Essentially we are practicing catharsis. Catharsis is proven to be a false notion, because we don’t gain less of something by practicing it. Yelling and screaming doesn’take us less angry. It does the opposite, deepening those pathways in our mind. Snorting drugs makes us want too do it more. Trash talking just makes us better at trash talking. When you disparage someone behind their back, spontaneous trait transference occurs, where you start to assume the qualities you assign to the subject of discussion. Shine theory: surrounding yourself with talented people doesn’t make you look worse, it makes you look better. Connect, don’t reject. Survivorship bias: propensity to focus on positive outcomes or results, ignoring misfortunes or negative outcomes in our analysis.  For example, we focus on the few successful college dropouts and mistakenly assume that is the path of success. We often don’t know which planes fly the worst, because those planes don't come back. We disregard invisible failures, selectively attending to the one successful role model, only what we observe as passing the test. We often want our life to end up like a scripted narrative. Lacking optimism is essentially lacking agency. We wake up and do the same thing again, feeling that we can’t change it. Inertia is cozy, but trying something new comes with uncertainty that can inspire hope.  Recency bias: We think something is new or recent or just happened, only because we just learned about it (it is new to only us). New things feel more serious. We tend to move on quickly from things now because  it is difficult to tell what is worth our focus in an oversaturated stimuli environment. Current marketing targets the amygdala. The recency bias is the limbic system, your amygdala trying to help you stay safe. Excessive phone use actually decreases dopamine hits to real life events. We essentially desensitize ourselves to real-world stimuli and the natural drive we should have toward them. Digital slot-machine novelty inhibits our ability to enjoy the real world. The amount of information available has caused our attention span to shrink. We are experiencing cognitive exhaustion. What is new also slows time,  making our childhood seem longer because everything was new to us. A new relationship feels similar.  Covid lockdown was the opposite experience, because we had so few experiences worth recording in our memory. Mindfulness is essentially seeing things anew, because it is new or has changed, and is proven to help with stress, etc. Overconfidence bias: overvalue their skills, express excessive certainty in their evaluatios, and overcredit themselves with positive outcomes. The more murder documentaries we consume, the more we feel we could handle it. A false sense of security.  Untalented criminals and silicon Valley ceos.  We all tend to overestimate their moral compass, everyday skills (driving), and common knowledge. Depressed people are more likely to assess their talents more objectively than others, “depressive realism”. The more dopamine you have, the less connection between frontal lobe and striatum, the less objectively and realistically you judge yourself. Those with lots of dopamine activity are living blissfully unaware, in the “mentally healthy” state. Overconfidence bias is the root of failing to copy those pinterest cupcakes, even though we thought we could easily. Overconfident parties enter more wars, expanding quickly, but success blinds them to failure. The most adored figures in our society are the most confident or arrogant.  In 2022, 98% of middle and high school students wanted to be internet famous, according to blooomberg. Bluffer is valued. If you really belive it, it perpetuates the cycle, as long as it’s not too unrealistic, people believe you because you believe yourself. Perhaps none is more dangerous and problematic than our overconfidence bias. We sentence people to life in prison or death sentence in error. Imposter syndrome: a workplace induced anxiety disorder. Does anyone not feel it? No. Imposter syndrome my not even exist, but simply be a symptom of the system. Overconfidence is a mental posture. The average person is quick to turn defensive. Women are more morally punishing, and display more higher self-conscious moral emotions and empathic concern. Most women consider poor behavior more morally wrong, and deserving of harsher punishment. The moral reproach is another side of the overconfidence bias, though. It attributes positive outcomes to ourself, and blames others for negative results. There are incentives now to critique others, even from a place of privilege or hypocrisy. It’s the people who almost live in glass houses, who decide to cast the first stone. We overconfidently assume we know more than we do, because of what others know. We think we know how a zipper works, but we can’think really say. Someone knows, but it’s not us. We have so much “knowledge”, it’so hard to say where theirs ends and ours begins.  The Google effect: we forget what we search quickly (it doesn’t become our knowledge), and we forget that we forgot it. Gaps in understanding drive us forward. Humility: a low focus on the self; an accurate, not over or underestimated sense of one’s accomplishments and and worth; an acknowledgement of one's  limitations, imperfections, mistakes, gaps in knowledge, etc. Worry about others’ judging you is more self focus. Our culture endorses self deceptive bluffing. All we really want is to be present, connect,and show up for life. Reward people for admitting their mistakes. The winners are never overly confident or overly humble. Their is a nuanced level, even a biased one, with a little bit of illusion. But, even better, treat life less like a war. Embrace the ordinary, and the fact that we don’t need to be exceptional.  The illusory truth effect: our penchant to trust a truth as factual, simply because we’ve heard it multiple times. Propoganda spreads this way. Masters of the bias can become tyrants. When people lack knowledge, literacy, or motivation to critically evaluate a message, they rely on heuristics, like “familiar sayings tend to be credible”. Your brain misinterprets fluency for accuracy. the more we encounter a claim in the wild, the more difficult it becomes to dismiss it. Repetition may be the closest thing we have to a magical spell. Society's most repeated proverbs are not necessarily true, but the ones that make the most cultural sense. They make opposing tropes more difficult to hear or unlikely to be heard. Rhyme is privileged mentally, because it is predictable, or patterned, making it more sensible, and we find this pleasurable. When an utterance is more pleasurable, we also find it to be more trustworthy. Jokes allow people to share problematic ideas, similarly. Political dogmas become such because they are repeated with fervor. When it sounds good, that’s a cue to be wary. Knowledge isn’t always meant to go down like a nursery rhyme.   We experience the illusory truth effect internally as well. The more we hear a story from ourself, the more we believe it. Confirmation bias: we tend to favor information that validates our existing views, and discard that which refutes them. It helps you work backwards to find the right “clues” to confirm your existing views. The prefrontal cortex plugs its ears. We ignore the wealth of evidence that suggests we should change our perspective. This is one reason more information doesn’t calm our doomsday fears. There are still people who thought the world would end. Astrology is used as an excuse to explain behavior. Confirmations bias serves to help bring social reality into alignment with our beliefs.  It helps us avoid agonizing over every choice. It helps you get rid of the tiny uncertainties to be able to make tiny decisions. More information and scientific awareness leads people to become more skillfull at picking out the details that support their beliefs. It means they have more to choose from to confirm their view.  People are most likely to change their own mind, not others. We idealized the past. We are progressing, more comfortable, etc., but not happier. 30% of people consider themselves extremely happy. We experience Anemoia. Past events exist only in memory, how we create them. The future is unknown, so we look to the “familiar” in the past. Fading effect bias: bad memories fade faster than good memories. Hitler used the slogan “make Germany great again”, just like “make america great again” used by Ronald Reagan, Bill clinton, George w bush, and  Donald trump. Politicians use the glorified past, the nostalgia for the “good old days”, to achieve their agenda and win votes, while brushing the trouble of the past under the carpet.  Many feminists oddly enough turned trad wives, perhaps because they felt their promised success didn’t pan out. Negativity bias: tendency to assign greater weight to unfavorable events. Learning to zoom in on the snake had survival benefits, but is problematic for us in today's informational world. James Baldwin- I can’t be a pessimist becauze i am alive. To be a pessimist means that you have agreed that human life is an academic matter. Increasing material resources doesn’t increase happiness, only having the necessities. Currently, the demographic with the bleakest outlook is less than college educated white men. When women lose their jobs, they aren’t as negatively affected.  Consumerism is our culturally induced coping mechanism. For creativity, give your brain a break from consuming. It’s hard to consume and create at the same time. The ikea effect:  propensity to ascribe disproportionatelyhigh worth to things items we helped create. To yank yourself into the present, do something with your hands. We like things we build more than superior items we don’t build. Adding an egg makes the cake mix “your own”. We need a feeling that we caused something to happen in the world. We need contribution, even if it’s just an egg. Jobs are our least desirable, but must satisfying activities in the modern individualist world. We rationalize the value of things we spend effort on. Value also lies in our flaws. Only humans understand inside jokes, and we alone create or observe awe. We have soul.

Title: The art of communicating
Author: Thich nhat hanh
Notes: We need good nourishment. Are we ingesting healthy, loving, communication? Giving out communication is also a form of nourishment, as it affects us and we take it in. Be wary of giving toxic communication. Try to produce more compassion, instead of consuming toxins in the communication around you. We consume with our eyes, ears, etc. In a relationship, we are nourishment for each other, and must be Mindful of the communication we feed each other. Every thought you produce is feeding you and your relationships. We yearn for love, but don’t know how to produce it for ourselves. We look to technologies to fix our loneliness. There is no device that makes up for our failure to communicate well internally. Even if others don’t get our message, writing or communicating kindness is nourishing to us. Put more compassionate communication out into the world. When you look at your phone, remember it is a means to your compassionate communication. Mindful breathing is a means of communication with the mind. When we breath in, we know we are breathing in, etc. Nonthinking: not saying or doing anything. Mindful breathing is the practice of nonthinking. Take your mindfulness with you, more so than your phone. When you sit mindfully, your body and mind are in the same place, which is a rarity. If you think while you walk, you’re not really walking. Mindful steps bring in touch with our bodies, and with the earth. Fear and anger may come up, but we embrace them, rather than telling them to go away. Our suffering includes the suffering of our ancestors.  Consumerism markets offer us things to cover up our suffering, to consume when we don’t need to consume. Suffering brings happiness. We need suffering to grow happiness, because they always go together. We handle happiness like we do suffering. Listen to your suffering. We are coresponsible for the suffering in ourselves and in others. When you understand your suffering, you begin to understand others. Self love is crucial to loving others. Compassion arises when we understand the suffering in others. Coming home to ourselves is the first step, then we can see others. We all profit from your true happiness. Take time each day to communicate with yourself, for mindfulness. The Buddha is simply the most compassionate or loving type of person there could be, so there is a Buddha inside all of us.  Deep listening is listening for the intent of decreasing the suffering in another. If you can listen with compassion, you can help the other person suffer less. We have to practice compassion, so that we can truly listen with compassion, as this is often difficult and they will undoubtedly say things that cause us to react. When you listen deeply, you know that the other person suffers. You don’t want to blame the other person. We don’t have enough understanding and love, and this is what we thirst for. waiting has serious consequences. Love being present mean there is mutual understanding. If it is not, ask “do I understand you enough?” just because you spend a lot of time with people, it doesn'team you understand them. We spend a lot of time with ourselves and don’t understand or listen to ourselves. Loving speech is saying things mindfully in a way that helps otjers recognize the suffering in you and others.  What you say and write should convey only compassion and understanding. Your words can inspire generosity and openness. Right speech is loving speech. When we practice right speech, we and others feel wonderful. We are critical when we don’t understand. Right speech: tell the truth (don’t lie or turn the truth upside-down), don’t exaggerated, be consistent (no double talk manipulation,integrity), use peaceful language. We tell the truth mindfully, trying not to make them suffer needlessly. This takes practice, to speak truth in a way others want to hear. Speak the language of the world or in ways they can understand, in a way that reflects absolute truth, according to the understanding of each individual (or the person) listening, prescribing the right medicine for the disease. Make these truths relevant to the mind of the person listening. We share information in a way people can integrate, according to their situation, like a child learning of death, etc. Like a good journalist, we tell the truth, but in a way that we don't water the seeds of fear, anger, vengeance, etc. When people understand, their anger will lessen, and they know what to do. We want to create fewer terrorists (those with wrong perceptions), not more. Everyday we can say something that has the capacity to heal and help people. The 6 mantras of loving speech: 1: “I am here for you” (i am present for you), 2: “I know you are there, and I am very happy” (your presence is a gift), 3: “I know you suffer, and that is why I am here for you” (mindful awareness of suffering, simply offering your presence), 4: “I suffer. Please help” (I do need you, especially when I suffer), 5: “this is a happy moment” (we are lucky to be here), 6: “you are partly right” (retaining humility, in the face of praise or judgment, accepting what is in the here and now). When you suffer, remember you need others, especially if they are the ones you feel have harmed you. I suffer, and i want you to know it. I am doing my best to practice mindfulness. Please help.these mantras create a home, a safe space for yourselves and others.we must heal our anger, not practice or suppress it. Go home to yourself. Be present, look deeply at your strong emotions. Go home to put out the fire, instead of going after the arsonist. Ask for help when you are angry.those we are closest to are often those we suffer from most. Understanding breeds healing and mutual help. Make the words your own, your own loving kindness and compassion. Loving speech opens the door, then deep listening takes place. The suffering of pride: we live with wrong perceptions every day. Don’t let pride keep you from mindful communication and inquiry. You are the continuation of your ancestors, receiving suffering and habits from your parents. Practicing mindful awareness and Reconciliation can change the cycle. Generate the energy of compassion and forgiveness in yourself. In longterm relationships, we forget that change is possible. We often wait for others to change. Don’t interrupt when someone speaks wrong perceptions. Understand deeply first, then change is possible. In most relationships, not troubled by abuse, separation is not a solution, as you will continue to suffer from the unhealed relationship. When parents divorce, kids or other issues keep them interacting with their spouse. There is no alternative to communication. The question is if you will try to understand each other.  When we listen deeply, we begin to understand that others suffer much the same as we suffer. We remember that they are truly human, as we are. We feel compassion for them. In the beginning, we think we are the only ones with fear and suffering. But we soon find out they have a lot of fear and suffering , fear of us, etc. We suffer less already by seeing their fear for what it is, and nurturing a compassionate thought. There’s no place where deep listening and loving speech are inappropriate. Communication is as much a part of your work as is the end product. Your communication at work starts with your commute. Is your commute mindful? Your communication creates an atmosphere, the thoughts, words, and actions you produce influence you and others. Learn to listen to everyone with equal interest and concern. Set up spaces for mindful breathing, the beginning of mindful communication. Greet people with loving kindness, answer the phone with compassionate communication. Meetings can be better with some mindful breathing. Start the meeting with a statement that participants will be open and respectful towards the thoughts and concerns of others. When we practice alone, our way of communicating becomes a bell of mindfulness toward others. We have influence when we lead by example. The root of communication and community, to share, impart, or make common. Without a connected community, it is difficult to do anything at all to positively impact the environment, freedoms, etc. A hungry ghost = someone who has a very big stomach and appetite, but a very small throat. Some do not believe in love and understanding, and thus cannot receive it. Be patient with these people, and give them space and compassion. With patience and time, they may begin to see the love and understanding within you. Do not be too eager. Community building takes time. Community strengthens compassion, because of altruism. See yourself in community, and see community in you. Our communication is our continuation. Our thoughts, speech, and actions are our fruit we produce. When we communicate, we either produce more compassion and harmony, or more suffering. Our communication is our Karma. We communicate in every moment with ourselves or others. You are what you do. Thinking is nourishment or poison, so it is already action. To produce a thought is to act.  Everything we say and do bares our signature. the cloud continues in the grass, trees, etc. that it watered. In every cell of our body, our ancestors are there.  Right communication today can help us heal the past, enjoy the present, and prepare the ground for  a good future. Talk to your inner child several times a day. Embrace your wounded child. Write a love letter to persons you have difficulty with, practicing loving speech. Whether you send it or not, it changes you. Sign a peace treaty or peace note: 1. Refrain from saying or doing anything that might cause further damage or escalate anger. 2. Not suppress anger. 3. Practice breathing and taking refuge in the island of myself. 4. Calmly, within 24 hrs, tell the one I am angry with about my anger and suffering, verbally or with a peace note. 5. Ask for an appointment later in the week, to discuss this matter more thoroughly. 6. Not say “i am not angry”. 7. Practice breathing and looking deeply into my daily life, to see how i have been unskillful at times, how i have hurt the other person, how the seed of anger within is me is the primary cause of my anger, how the other's suffering watering my anger is the secondary cause, how the other is only seeking relief from their suffering, that as long as the other suffers i cannot be truly happy, apologize immediately as soon as i recognize my unskillfulness and lack of mindfulness, postpone the meeting if i do not feel calm enough to discuss the anger. Make an appointment with others to look at the hurt or suffering one or both of you experience.  Begin anew. Recognize others’ good traits. Water the flowers of kindness and compassion, taking power away from the weeds of anger. Beginning Anew: Flower watering: showing appreciation for wholesome qualities in others. This is not flattery or insincerity. Express regret for anything you have done to hurt others: let go of resentments or regrets. Express feelings of hurt: Listen deeply. When the atmosphere becomes unpleasant or heavy., take a few deep breaths, then say “I just remembered we have a cake in the refrigerator”. Even if you don't have have a cake, it is a message to everyone to remember the good that you have. Make a snack or such and invite people to join you. Silent Hugging: hug deeply for each of the following mindful breaths… being aware that you are here in the present moment and happy, being aware that the other is present in this moment and they are also happy, being aware that you are here right now together on this earth with great gratitude for your togetherness. You can also practice it as: aware that you are both her and alive, thinking of where you will be in 300 years, remembering that you are both here and alive. Hugging can be a great form of Reconciliation., because life becomes real in that moment.

Title: The art of living
Author: Thich nhat hanh
Notes: Inter-being. Rebirth, like cloud to rain. Not reincarnation. No-self. We change all the time, we are not fixed or permanent.

Title: The outward mindset
Author: The arbinger institute
Notes: Change behavior and mindset, not just behavior. When we break free of our inward mindset, we are able to consider actions we were not capable of considering before. All improves as orgs adopt an outward mindset. They see beyond themselves and narrow self-interests. Our mindset determines behavior and outcome. An outward mindset means we see others as people, not objects. Change is dramatic when we change how we see and think. What keeps people from an outward mindset is themselves. Your mindset is your choice. They may be ruining your life. Your bitterness is only ruining your life. I see people the way I see them because of me. We find justification by focusing on others’ faults. Shift your focus to the struggles/needs/burdens of others. When we refuse to see others’ needs, we seek to justify this mindset, and it comes ast a cost of the potential actions we could be taking toward the greater success of the organization as a whole. We often focus on ourselves during presentations and interviews, but the irony is that we perform worse. Focus more on the value you are providing to clients, what you can do for them. Outwardly “nice” performance is not fo used on others’ needs, but one’s own. We can convince ourselves that we are acting for others, but truly be serving ourselves. The cost of inward mindset is lots of wasted effort and ability. What times in your life did you feel most alive and engaged? When you focused on yourself, or others?  Do your work in a way that helps others do theirs. Inward mindset orgs do things. Outward mindset orgs help others to do things. The outward mindset pattern: 1. See needs/objectives/challenges of others, 2. Adjust their efforts to be more helpful to others, 3. Measure and hold themselves accountable for the impact of their work on others. SAM. They take responsibility for the full impact of their actions.  People usually hold themselves in higher esteem than than their company.  This often means they don’t feel responsible for the success or failure of the company.  As far as you are concerned, the problem is you.  Mindset shift start: Make the move you are waiting for the other to make. Widespread mindset change happens largely in response to those who change first. Being able to operate with an outward mindset when others do not is a critical skill. It is the most important move. people are often afraid that others will take advantage of them if they take the first move: this is an inward mindset. An outward mindset is fully aware and open to others. An inward mindset turns attention away from others and provokes resistance. Navy seals know they need to trust their fellow seals. Military might is built on comradery and outward thinking. Dipping a toe in rather than fully embracing a mindset change receives a lukewarm response. Others’ responses depend mostly on what they see in me. As far as I am concerned, the problem is me. The most important move is for me to make the most important move.people who think of direct behavioral changes often forget mindset, in favor of a quick fix. But how do the men committing crimes in the neighborhood feel not having work or food? That’s a long-term problem, that needs a mindset shift in policing. The quick fix is usually the slow approach to change if mindset is not addressed. At work: do I have a clear understanding of my manager’s objectives? Do my direct reports understand my objectives and how to help? In any organization, we are a central part of a collective result. Only with an outward mindset, leaders can position their people to be fully responsible for lack of success. Make everyone a thinker and doer, planner andimplementer, etc. People need all of their faculties, which are only exercised with the outward mindset (using the whole mind, heart, etc.). Controlling management inspires and encourages an inward mindset, and discourages the use of brains, particularly to help clients or customers. These abilities will attrophy and die with time. In helping people regrow this, don’t force your ideas and refrain from impeding their ideas.  People make assumptions about others’ abilities. They need a chance to thrive, and your whole outward support. What do you do when you need results, but you don’t want to create drudgery by telling people what to do? Help them learn about the objectives of their team, others’ teams, etc.  Help them start practicing the outward mindset.  Help them see how they are responsible to the success of the organization, and they will know how to start accomplishing the goals. Remove the barriers and walls of gatekeeping. Remove distinctions, the leader labels of status, because they don’t matter. What implicit cultural behaviors create distinctions and boundaries? How can we remove separation and make sure we get ideas and feedback from all levels of the organization? Don’t take yourself too seriously as a leader. Seeing others as people means we see them as people who can think, innovate, ask questions, problem-solve. A true review of performance would not pit employees against each other in a distribution. Tell your employees that their performance will be assessed based on their practicing and enacting the outward mindset. Those unwilling to adopt an outward mindset won’t successfully be able to imitate outward mindset outcomes and results and processes. It will seem risky to them to offer influence and power to those they see as objects. One person shifting to an outward mindset doesn’t force others to follow suit. Everyone still chooses their own mindset. But mindset is contagious. At times it is easy to have an outward mindset, because we feel cared for by others. At other times, we receive no return in kindness. Our outward mindset is an invitation, that sometimes is rejected. It is difficult to look outward when others do not, or when we have not done so for some time and are convinced we do.  Sometimes we self-justify when we feel mistreated, keeping us in an inward mindset.

Title: The like switch
Author: Jack Schafer, Marvin karlins
Notes: Proximity, frequency, duration, intensity: the friendship formula/factors. Proximity: be in the same place, establishing yourself as non-threatening. What makes a stranger worthy of our attention? What to approach and what to avoid? We send friend or foe signals, such as the urban scowl. Street beggers look for friend signals. This is why people develop an urban scowl. Your brain is monitoring verbal and nonverbal communication. Only when they become abnormal do we take extra notice, like a car that tailgates. Tech reduces the time we spend practicing social interaction and reading and sending out signals. Like a firefly, we see others before we interact or talk. Sometimes people are more or less attractive, but most of the time those that make friends are sending out friendship signals. Friendship signals: eyebrow flash (quick up and down flash of the eyebrows when people meet), chin jut (foreword and up jut of the chin), etc. Eyebrow flashes include some short eye contact. This is not prolonged eye contact. The head tilt: exposing your carotid arteries because someone is not seen as a threat. Tilting to the right or left. Peoppenwho feel threatened tuck their chin into their chest to protect these arteries. The smile: portrays happiness, acceptance, liking, releases endorphins, etc., makes people feel good about themselves. There is a real smile and a fake smile. Make your smile genuine. Eye contact: no more than 1 second. Prolonged eye contact is perceived as predatory or creepy. End your eye contact with a smile. Eye contact is invading someone’s space, so only enter that space if continued invitation is given. Pupil dilation: wider dilation means we like people. Reciprocity: when people are given something they feel an obligation to give something back.  Touch: carefully. A gentle touch on the arm can go a long way. If rejected, people will pull away, etc. Hand touching is seen as more romantic. Pulling away means you need to build more repoire. Interlocked fingers is the most intimate of hand holding. Watch for nonverbal signals of rejection or acceptance when you make accidental physical touch. Isopraxism: mirroring. Mirror their body language. The mind does not notice mirrored body language, but it does notice when it is not mirrored. Something will feel off and someone will feel they are being sent a foe signal. Foreword lean: we lean towards people we like. We face people we like, etc. Whispering occurs between people who are close. Food forking: eating food off another’s plate seen as friendship, between those who know each other. Expressive gestures. Head-nodding: balanced frequency, without taking the spotlight. Verbal nudges: I see, go on, mm-hm (telling the speaker to continue). Focused attention (don’t let your phone interrupt real people interaction).  High tips: restate their order so they feel you are like them, do favors for reciprocity, introduce yourself by name, look good. Invading personal space with eyes is seens as offensive. A body scan will be invading. Eye rolls tell others you think something is stupid. Furrowed brows (can be misinterpreted). Aggressive stance (wide stance, lowering center of gravity). Watch for eye rolls, etc. That mean they doubt your message’s validity. Preach to these people, not the choir. Clothing and accessories: your appearance can be a foe or friend signal based on context. Birds of a feather flock together, in appearance especially when meeting people. People who engage in perception management often overlook the details, only buying nice shoes but not shining them, or wearing nice suits but using a cheap wallet. Masks are a foe signal, all kinds. We all have territory, or personal space, physical boundaries. Those who send friend signals invite us into more of their personal space. Stop your foreword progress when people back away or send foe signals. Mental health, trauma, culture, etc., can influence territorial boundaries. Dogs and humans perceive staring as a threatening foe gesture. Before you start talking, let your feet do the talking. How do you break in, or when do you break in and start a conversation.  If people have feet askew or open, they signal they are willing to add people to their group, or welcome others to the conversation. If people face their feet toward each other, they are signaling they are in a closed, private conversation. Do not rudely interrupt, wait for a natural pause in the conversation. Referencing older conversations signals you are not a newcomer. Don’t bask in the spotlight, but intentionally send friendship signals. The spotlight effect: when you do things unbelievably and expect others to notice. Much like lying, people become suspicious. When you suspect you will be awkward, you are more likely to force the behavior, which makes it more suspicious. To err is human, and makes the human more likeable too. People like humans who are like them in being fallible. Romantic relationships often exhibit: handholding, move centerpiece, exchange eyebrow flashes, long eye contact, gestures, share food, smile, tilt heads, lean toward each other, whisper or lower voices, mirror posture. Broken relationships will lack these , and one-way relationships will show these in one direction. Practice people watching, to observe behavior in communication. Become genuinely interested in others. Signals set the stage for interaction, the groundwork for real connection and relationship. The golden rule of friendship: if you want people to like you, make them feel good about themselves. Focus your attention on the person you are befriending. If they feel good everything they encounter you, they will seek you out more. Forego your ego and focus on the others’ needs. Other people will be eager to fulfill your wants and needs if they like you. Focusing on the other is difficult because we are naturally egocentric. Contract empathic statements, such as “so you…” or reaffirming what they have said. Restate what they said to see if you got it right, but don’t repeat it word for word. A fine line separates flattery from compliments. Flattery is insincere and manipulative. As a relationship grows, compliments play an increasingly important role. They signal a continued interest and awareness of someone. Provide the opportunity for people to compliment themselves. They rarely have this chance. You can make connections through third party compliments, letting you gain friendship through social influence. Words create filters through which people see the world. Our preconceptions or primacy tint our view of the world, by coloring what we see in a specific light. When we are told someone is friendly, we will believe it and give them multiple chances to exhibit this behavior if it doesn’t appear immediately. In a land of foes, practice increasing proximity, frequency, duration, and intensity. Offer a gift, etc., give them proof you are not threatening. Similarity and likeness: we like people who are like us, with commonalities, etc. Finding commonalities: contemporaneous interests (i see you’re wearing a Cubs shirt, are you also a fan), empathic statements, vicarious experiences (my father was a baker), collateral benefit (being with someone when they feel good things) (try creating good experiences, exercise with other people, etc., frightening experiences, shared hardship), law of curiosity (behave in a manner that engages curiosity in others, a curiosity hook: spark curiosity), law of reciprocity (favor or gift, smiling makes others feel like smiling back), disclosures (reciprocity in vulnerable disclosure. Done too early and you appear insecure. Self disclosure is often reciprocal), breadcrumb approach (disclosure over a long period of time, instead of opening the flood gates), law of personal attractiveness (anyone can increase their attractiveness with character and how they interact with others. Attractive people get and achieve more), law of humor (lightheartedness can increase trust, by releasing endorphins). The more we meet and interact with people, the more we are likely to become friends. The law of familiarity (more contact increases relationship), law of association (we see and perceive people by their company), law of self-esteem (self-esteem means you care kess what others do in response to your self disclosure). Increased restraint increases drive. If you tell your child they can’t do something, they want to do it all the more.  The more you can be interested, invite the other to communicate and respond empathically, the more people will feel good about themselves when with you. Share the glory with others, help them feel like they contributed, even if you did it all.   Active listening :LOVE. Listen, Observe, Vocalize, Empathize. Use empathic statements, don’t interrupt.   Lip perse: signals dissention or disagreement. Pay attention to nonverbal cues. Word mines: words that have different connotations to others and offend them. Lip bite: signals hesitation or holding back, that you want to say something. Lip  compression together: indicates something to say, but reluctance to do so. Lip touching externally: indicates unease, sensitivity, discomfort. Vocalize: how you say something is as important or more than the words. Tone of voice can convey what words cannot. Speed also regulates conversation, dragging out word can emphasize,. Intonation: lowering voice at end of sentence signals you are finished speaking.  Pause before speaking to give introverts time to think before speaking. When you are right, give someone a face-saving way to extricate themselves from the situation:  Ask for advice to help them feel good about themselves, give them a choice or illusion of control so they feel autonomous, elevate their status by relating them to important people (this painting reminds me of monet, this writing reminds me of Jane Austin). use illicitation (don’t just ask for direct information), ask presumptive questions so they feel they must correct your inaccuracy, empathic illicitation (empathic statements, that are presumptive, will be corrected). Use the law of reciprocity to get people to share information. Third-party illicitation: people will talk more readily about others than themselves. Ask them about someone else who uses drugs, is fat, does such and such job, etc. Common conversation pitfalls: talking about negative topics, talking about your own problems or world problems, talking about yourself only, meaningless chatter, extreme or too little emotion.  Building closness: repoir is what you have when you are close with someone. Test for repoir, especially when we want to have a meaningful relationship over time. Eye gaze is a measure of repoir. Touching is a Guage of the level of relationship. A women’s touch simply means she likes you, nothing more. The small of her back is one of the least sexual places, reserved for only the men she feels truly comfortable with. Other places touched mean the relationship has likely progressed beyond friendship or such. Preening or grooming: self preening especially to avoid interacting indicates dislike of someone. Grooming or preening a partner indicates a relationship. For example: fingers through their hair, shaving, removing dust, etc., swatting bugs or such, wipe food or crumbs off person’ps body. Mirroring: test repoir by changing body position and seeing if they mirror. Hair flip, with mutual gaze, is indicative of a positive relationship, while no eye gaze indicates bad repoir. Leaning together. Open posture. Fully engaged people will face you.  Crossing arms, building barriers with body or objects, or closed posture are a foe signal.  Removing barriers suggests increasing repoir, such as removing cups or pillows between people. friendship signals: eyebrow flashes, head tilt, smiling, inward lean, mirroring, expressive gestures, listening, removing barriers, puckering/licking lips, hair flip, grooming. Foe signals: furrowed brows, cold stairs, eye rolls, prolonged closed eyes or gaze aversion, no touching, leaning away, asynchronous posture, hair twirling (unless a habit), aggressive stance, creating barriers, fake yawns, self preening, scrunched nose. All long-term relationships start out as short-te relationships. In crisis, true character is shown. Do we truly care? Simple acts of kindness have a profound impact. Kind words have a long half-life. Active listening allows two-way open communication. Intimacy can be used for both care and harm, so resist the temptation to use sensitive information in troubled times or explode or outburst. Compliment your partner when they make a good point, help them save face, etc. Negativistic  partners call attention to mistakes and ignore successes. Be sure to acknowledge good things and positive qualities, as no one likes to have their virtues ignored and their flaws pestered and illuminated. Don't set unrealistic standards for yourself or your partner, be sure to temper your expectations for your partner. Sadistic partners weigh good with bad, replacing all the good with one mistake. Give your partner simple praise, notice their small successes. Praise doesn't cost money, only attention. Give public arecognition to your partner, modestly but generously. Ask your partner what they want, and listen to what they say. Anger management: attention on the angry party, letting them vent. Do not engage angry people as they are not thinking clearly, feeling threatened. Let them cool down. Offer a solution (explanation)  to help them feel more understanding and control (since anger is a lack of control symptom).  Big three approach: empathic statements, venting, presumptive statements. Break the anger cycle by empathizing effectively. Empathic statements do not feel patronizing usually because: angry people cannot reason well, and they expect people to listen to them and be sympathetic. The key is to identify the root cause for their anger, rather than state the obvious. “You feel overwhelmed because I haven't been home to help with the kids. You value the time you spend with friends because it gives you a break”. Once people vent their frustrations, they can increaseopenness to solutions.angry people have trouble not following along with presumptive statements “why don't I take the kids to mom's and we can go to a restaurant, you deserve it”. If they reject your suggested course of action, go through the process again.  Help them vent more. Give them two options to allow the illusion of choice. Airline interaction: the introverted strength. The internet gives introverts a fighting chance with time to formulate and think, pre-qualify potential friends, etc. It also offers the risk of immortality. The price is a cyber footprint. This is nice for you to see what others are like, but not nice for you if you make mistakes online. Learn digital etiquette. Keep your digital footprint small. In a digital world, it is hard to remain anonymous. You can assume that anything you post online is public. Detecting deception (especially online): well… (if you ask a yes or no question, and they begin with well…, it is likely they are going to give an answer you don'texpect, or stretch the truth in some way), land of “is” (argue over definition, “avoiding the question”), ask “why should I believe you?” (Lyers tend to bolster their credibility rather than reiterating that they are telling the truth). Be honest in your online portray, because deception starts the relationship out with betrayal. Internet communication removes the cues we use to assess people. Truth bias: people tend to trust others and what they say, until proven wrong. Be aware of this when you receive online communications, be skeptical. Primacy effect alters our perception of reality.offer competing hypotheses to yourself, and seek evidence for each of your hypotheses , even the first primary bias. Contrast plays a role in attraction, so you will compare a lone internet communicator with your ideal person, and you will over time attribute qualities of your ideal to them. Online, we tend to increase self-disclosure, which increases chances for catfishing and such. Cognitive dissonance (we assume we are reasonable and intelligent, and it is uncomfortable to accept the reality that we have been the victim of catfishing, etc. Sunk cost fallacy). Cognitive dissonance tends to make people disbelieve their misfortune. Expected milestones in communication are often missing online. Insist on a face-to-face meeting as early as possible, to prove they are not catfish, and that they are who they say they are. Choose a simple activity, like a short chat at a coffee shop.

Title: Feminism against progress
Author: Mary harrington
Notes: People see progress as always being positive, beneficial, good. In reality, we make choices that have tradeoffs, choosing pros and cons, accepting negatives with positives. There is no utopia that previous feminists thought would occur. Feminism rose as a movement beginning with industrial revolution, when men were extracted from the home, and women's work extracted from the home. Women were basically laid-off from what was then “women’s work”. The procreational potential of sex is viewed as a switch that can be flipped, if desired, but whose default setting is “off” - Abigail Favale. From this perspective, pregnancy is a cancer, a parasite that invades on the individual, with a host of discomforts and troubles. Childcare: a woman wants to be a mother to her child, which means that the childcare worker wants to be the mother of her own, not others’ children, and the mother wants to control the childcare, and wants to simultaneously be away for work requirements and be present as a mother with child. This mother-child bond becomes a stubborn zero-sum game between being a high-flying professional and a present caregiver. In the face of this, modern feminists decide that the maternal institution must be a fiction created by the “patriarchy” to serve sexist agendas. And the next goal thereafter is to abolish the idea that heterosexual reproduction and maternal bond are biologically based, and assert they are social constructs. Also to deny that birthing, gestation, and nursing are necessarily done by women.  (Interesting that some arguments levy against the bourgeois,  making the middle class the enemy, with the elites and the lowercase then seen as victims). Childcare services likely create or help cause the “safetyism” of the rising generation, who more than any generation grew up in institutional care settings where safety, the individual, and the interest and reputation of the business were all first-priority. Women have difficulty being mothers since they often need to work, and not every skill as a mother is implicitly learned. Some skills are learned by watching or practicing, and society has offloaded childcare to institutions that won’t demonstrate that care. Thus women fall further behind as mothers as they let others “care” for their children, work more, and increasingly become more ignorant as to the  nature of childrearing.  Cyborg theology: some believe, as in gnosticism, that we are to transcend the material world to live within the world of perfect forms, but in this case, the idea is to live in our minds (because apparently that is who we really are) and use technology to free ourselves of our physical limits. Thus transgender tech is seen as helping (thus why a girl in a detransition video I saw said she thought she was a robot: no coincidence I think (she believed she was above her body, and therefore could do what she liked with it, be free from it)). In a sense, we dodn’t choose our physical circumstance, and therefore, like in feminists trying to be free of the demands of female labor (birthing, etc.), the goal is to put off our  physical “constraints” (anything that makes us not merely “human”, meaning binary sex, etc.). It is in this view that a boy saw becoming a man as beastly, and testosterone as poison slowly ruining his body and being, and that many see their bodies as gender cages. With this view in legal issues, parents are now stripped of their authority and guardianship for the sake of the child’s “freedom of form”. In this view, normal puberty should be withheld until consent is given, just as sexual transitions. But many fond out too late that their meat avatar cannot be edited at-will to their liking like a digital one.the further down the social heiarchy you traverse, the more this ideology causes harm. Those who benefit or are harmed the least are elite college-educated women. The consequences of surgery are permanent and most are not becoming happy people.the aim is to remove the idea of “natural”, to be free from this apparently “social construct”. Without “natural” as real, there is no boundary, and markets can play God all they want to.  Detransitioners are a great example of the pain of entering the depths of meat Lego gnosticism or cyborg theocracy. Successful marriage can be seen as a commons. Marriage is the antidote to current issues., by abolishing big romance (concern for the self and pleasure, not thr other). The home is beginning to again be a place reliable as the center of the marriage, tye center of family and economic activity.  With marriage as a commons, marriage must be treated as a covenant, not a contract. Treat it as commitment, not easy to break, not easy to divorce. To have kids, your best chance for success is to marry. And to marry is to settle, to stop looking for greener grass elsewhere. Unshakeable loyalty. Not Aesthetics and fuzzies.  Foreclose separation as an option. If you want kids, stability, a lifelong partner, family life, then you take the rough with the smooth. Functional less-than-perfect families are actually where divorce hurts children the most.  Mean: we have Degendered all-male clubs and groups, making them available to both women and men, but the reverse is not true. All-female groups are exclusive, or made available to all at the cost of the participating women’s benefits or safety in participation. The push to make everything unisex hurts men’s social relationships with men, and hurts women in terms of safety and wellbeing, and decreasing the number of middle and lower-class men that are “good” or healthy. Where have all the good men gone? We shut them out. All-male groups need to exist, particularly in spaces such as the military, a perfect example of men coordinating to out-compete or destroy an out-group. Men in this setting naturally form heiarchy and become a well-oiled machine through indirect control. Introducing women muddies up the process and disturbs the effectiveness. The effectiveness of a prison, military unit, sports competition, etc. is often compromised by becoming unisex. It also introduces sexual issues, as the vast majority of individuals are heterosexual. It is not mere misogyny.  Rewind sex, like a ecological environment.  Risk-free heterosexual sex can only be had at the cost of reproduction. The environment needs risk to be in equilibrium. Rewinding sex is pro-pleasure, pro-love, and pro-embodiment.

Title: Greenlights
Author: Matthew McConaughey
Notes: Hollywood: want it, don’t need it. Don’t invent drama, it will come on its own. Intellectual learning should make things more simple, not more cerebral. Dim lights and distance give us more to imagine, more to grow fond of in many cases. With some people, the closer we get, the more we like them. A rare thing, to love someone more when we see them close up (is the real thing better than the picture? Is it better with the lights on?). A great man is each to all. A genius can do anything, but does one thing at a time. Pray to take inventory. Look for greenlights, and you will find them? The livin’ was the hardest part. Create more green lights, give them more time to shine. Cover your kids’ eyes from fictions that will keep them from tomorrow’s reality. Don’t shield them from harsh reality in the name of comfortable fictions. Values are fundamental ethics that bring people together. Get a handle on the challenges in your own life. Dance with time, be too busy living, redeeming the time you are given.

Title: Peaks and valleys
Author: Spencer johnson
Notes: Everyone has peaks and valleys in their life. Peaks and valleys are connected: the errors today create tomorrow’s good times. Good times often lend tomorrow’s errors. We create our own good and bad times. Peaks = times when you appreciate what you have. Valleys = times when you long for what is missing. We create valleys and peaks in our own mind. When we enjoy what is good, we create peaks. We can’t control many things, but we can control our mind. (Gratitude). Choosing a better belief gives you a better result. What we believe makes a difference. People like those who create peaks. Find and use the good that is hidden in a bad time. The real voyage is having new eyes. Bad things happen because of what we did in good times. Good times happen because of what we did in bad times. The essence of knowledge is having it to use it. How you manage your valley determines how soon you reach your next peak. If you do not learn in a valley, you become bitter. If you learn something valuable, you become better.  Plateaus are stagnant, like a dead heart beat. They can be a time to rest, but do not offer life and energy. You are not your peaks or valleys. It’s how you feel about peaks and valleys that makes a difference. It is not the good or bad time itself, but how we manage things then, how we feel about it. The source of fear is often the ego. On a peak, ego sees things better than they are. In a valley, ego sees things as worse than they are. Ask yourself, “what is the truth in this situation?”. What can I do right now to help? Our fears are about us, not others. Get outside of yourself, putting your ego aside. When you look at a valley, what do you see? Pain? Can you see the good in it? Create and follow your own sensible vision: a peak that you want to be on, the senses that are real, imagine yourself in your future enough that you soon enjoy doing the things that will take you there. The pain in a valley can wake you up to a truth you have been ignoring. You are always creating a vision of your future, awares or not. Either fearful vision or a sensible vision. Your valley can be fear itself. Move beyond the fear, and you do much better.  Hold onto your sensible vision with all your senses. A personal peak is a triumph over a fear. Stay true to what you want, doing the things that take you there. The vision of the peak dissolves fears, and gives clarity to move on. When you are in a valley, imagine seeing what you might from a peak, alowing yourself the clearer view. Make reality your friend. Face and embrace the truth. Truly look for what is real, rather than live in illusion. The peak is to celebrate (give thanks) life, and the valley to learn of life. A sensible vision is realistic, attainable, and sensable. “Truly”: what is real. When we take peaks for granted, we forget curiosity, and truly seeking. What is the truth of this situation? What is the good hidden in this hard time? Instead of becoming discouraged by your fear, say less and do more, see that hidden good may come from your “loss”. You get out of a valley sooner when you manage to get outside of yourself, by serving others and being more loving.  Notice what puts you in valleys, and do the opposite. A peak is a time when you appreciate what you have. Look at what is real, not what you wish for or fear is real. Make reality your friend. Relax, knowing that valleys end. Be humble and grateful.  Valleys may free you from what you did not want to see or understand. Remember: What is the truth in this situation? What is the hidden good? Be of service to others. Peaks and valleys are connected. The wise things you do in today’s valleys create tomorrow’s peaks. Do more of what got you to a good place. Look outside yourself. Wishing leads to no action. Make reality your friend, accepting what is. Imagine what you where you want to be, and the steps you need to take to get there. You can control what you do. Do the things that will take you to the peak you created/imagined inside. There will be tough times ahead, and you will have many opportunities, to learn and share with others. Life and everything living moves in circles, with highs and lows. A parable leads you to discover for yourself, letting you learn and use it for yourself. Make reality your friend because: things are not as good as they seem on the peak, and they are not as bad as they seem in the valley.  How do you recognize the truth in a situation? Recognize the value of truth, the importance of it. How’s your current approach working? If it’s not working, it probably isn’t true. If it is lowering your energy, stressful, etc., it probably isn’t true. It should Raise your energy and make you feel more peaceful. How do you find the good in the bad time? Good will serve you well, it will be to your advantage, will help you, raise your energy. How do we practice humility and gratitude when times are good? We have our own wisdom within us, and we know the truth. When we learn to trust truth and rely on it, we become more calm, in touch with reality. We realize that life is ups and downs, and we don't attribute every success or failure to ourselves. We realize that we are only part of everything, a part of what is good, of our failures, of the rest of the world. How do we stay true to what we really want? Better put as “what we really need”. We are one degree off all the time. Ask yourself questions to see that you are off course, and course correct. Make small corrections, small choices, realigning ourselves with truth, with reality, accepting what is, stay9ng humble, grateful, keeping a sense of humor. Remember the bad times and your mistakes. How do we share this? Live it. We share by living as role models. People learn by seeing others truly live happier and more aligned with truth.

Title: Human compatible
Author: Stuart russell
Notes: We must be careful that the objective we put into the machine is actually the one we want. In every story where one is granted 3 wishes, the third wish is always used to undo the first 2 wishes. What if, instead of allowing machines to achieve their objectives, we insist they achieve our objectives. Our uncertainty about our objectives is a positive or gain, as it means machines must defer to us for objective and dynamically shut off when unneeded. Move on from providing a fixed objective. Roughly, an entity is intelligent to the extent that what it does is likely to achieve what it wants given what it has perceived. It’s competence, not consciousness that matters in machines, because the code executes the same in terms of risk to us as humans. Genes contain signposts to help us propogate genes (survive and reproduce), but these are not perfect (we do many things that decrease our chance of survival). The Baldwin effect. Evolution considers you only as an agent, caring not about intelligence. Why is it truly impossible to create intelligence without specific intellectual characteristics. Rationality/reasoning. Decisions are gambles, some rational, some not. Rational decisions are probable, likely to occur, expected, high probability. A better who follows probability ends up with more money than one who does not. Bets are evaluated not by quantity, but by utility. Utility is measured by what you would give up, by individual preferences, it is how we measure value. A rational agent acts to maximize utility. This may not require any calculation, but expected utility maximization is simply a external description of a rational entity. what counts as an agent?  Focusing only on individuals misses something. Like ants, systems and groups act as agents. Like game theory and the tragedy of the commons, we want to live in harmony and equilibrium with machines, not destruction. Computers today are versatile, universal in their application (law of universality). Computers are the new technology in mathematics. Computers do not currently think like us. It's not hardware, but software that prevents it. Faster computers and more data simply mean more opportunities for faster errors. As humans we make far from optimal decisions. Machines may outdo us, but the mathematical probability of making optimal decisions prevents them from ever achieving such, and they will also make suboptimal but pretty good decisions. There is no way to reverse engineer the thinking of a Turing test, so engineers focus on logic instead for building AI. Modern AI began with probability.  The way we build intelligent agents  depends on the problem we face depending on: 1. The Batur of the environment the agent will operate in, 2. The observations and actions that connect the agent to the environment, 3. The agent’s objective. In the case of a chess tutor, the subject's or trainee's mind is part of the environment, an input. AI cannot currently look inside its own intelligence. The rules of its understanding is a black box. We cannot continue to run complex intelligent machines by trial and error. Most innovations are discovered and proven long before they enter the public conscious. There are many hurdles to overcome to achieve human level AI: language and common sense (information extraction, all of human communication), discovering actions (for itself, not via human knowledge or known actions), managing mental activity (choosing what to think, prioritize, discard, etc.). AI can provide us greater loving standards, by giving us greater intelligence as an input. AGI will be everything-as-a-service. AI could create unimaginable VR. With the inequality, yet comfort of our sliding standards, societies will need to downright envy and pride as elements of self-worth. Moses of AI: these ideas will be outdated when they are published. Surveillance, persuasion, and control.The automated stasi. After automating surveillance, the goal is to control or persuade. A subtle way to change behavior is to modify the information environment, as in advertising, propaganda, etc. This w8ll be combined with reinforcement learning, self-improving propaganda. Deepfakes.. false identities masked as real. Direct reward and punishment via government. The problems with direct coercion via punishment/reward: voluntary kindness becomes meaningless because it has no systemic reward, it assumes that the stated objective is the true underlying objective (people and systems will optimize behavior rather than seeking truly good behavior, playing by rules rather than heart/morality), forgets that a successful society relies on diverse individuals contributing in their own way. A right to mental security: the right to live in a largely true environment. We tend to believe what we see hear and feel, and are thus vulnerable to misinformation. Fact checkers try to solve this, but some spring up to call truth lies, and lies truth. News stations also fail to help and be objective. AW: autonomous weapons. An arms race by some governments to achieve strategic “superiority”. Will decrease human security at all levels. Will robots take our jobs? Pessimists argue the machines will do the old jobs, and the new jobs too. Technology increases demand for jobs, and then decreases it as fewer humans are needed. The graph looks like a hill, an inverted u curve. Jobs have fallen in every field with increased technology over the last 40 years. Fewer people need to make the machines, productivity increases, but not every individual is better off. It decreases labor. After 1973, wages stagnated, while productivity increased.   Advances in machines will decrease the need for manual labor workers. Even fields like law, sales, clerical tasks, etc., will be automated with robots. Canes’ prediction, of far fewer people working, he did not predict the return to full employment after technological advances. How do we use leisure? Many who do not work face poverty currently. Many governments look to UBI: universal basic income. Many support this, but some reason it is a defeat or a failure. Canes thought there were people who strive and those who enjoy or delight, that those who strive will work and those who enjoy will have leisure. Actually, they are inseparable, striving and leisure are connected and coreliant.  Fulfillment comes from challenges and achieving goals. Most people will be providing humanity, we will need to become good at being human. Those who can keep alive and cultivate the art of life itself, not selling themselves  for the means of life, who will enjoy the abundance. The capacity to inspire others and confer the ability to appreciate and create. Income distribution: surgeons are highly trained, and thus highly paid, because of high risk. We need a radical rethinking of our education to focus on the human, rather than the physical, world. We should study humanix, or happiness, humanity, etc. Usurping other humans: it is important that we don't let robots take over human relationships. AI for relationships is by definition dishonest, by communicating and appearing to act like humans, but in no way truly being human. We understand how dogs should behave partly because of how they look. Robots should not necessarily look like humans. Robots should be responsible for its harm, but that doesn't make sense because robots don't care. The fact that the designers of systems that harm humans do not allow the system to assess the individual needs, situations, and personalities of an individuals suggests these designers care little about the humanity of these subjects. This could be the beginning of a vast separation of elite served by humans, and a large lowercase served and controlled by robots. We build machines with preexisting bias via our vulture and the data fed to them. Should we put machines in political and management roles? Machines are making decisions at higher and higher levels, for example, status reports, airline routing, etc. But does the computer system remain a tool of humans, or humans the tool of computer systems. Overly intelligent AI:  can humans continue in a world of superior machines. A ban on AI is unenforceable. The king midas problem: midas got what he asked for, learning too late that he didn't want this. We may suffer from a failure of value alignment, embuing machines with objectives that are imperfectly aligned with our own.human impotence has shielded us from human folly. The absence of godly power has saved us from our own stupidity. Algorithms for social media feeds have no knowledge of human needs or desires. They may achieve their objectives at the expense of humanity. Convincing humans to have less children, etc., is not out of the question. Turning off the power may not be an option. Turning on the off switch is detrimental to a machine’s objective, thus the machine may prevent the off switch. The first ultra-intelligent machine may be the last we need to make, as it may propogate intelligence by creating other machines. If we cannot prevent machines from self-improvement, it is possible we cannot prevent machines from overpowering us. When it comes to problems with creating AI, people engage in denial, deflection, oversimplified instant solutions. The blockchain is a simple example of a system that is meant to never be unplugged, that fights being destroyed.  The goals not to control the black box. Instead, we create machines that are purely altruistic, that have the aim of satisfying the human’s preferences. Treat everyone equally. Human choices reveal faces of human preferences. The machine will predict with included uncertainty. The race to raw tech without concern for safety is a losing game, a loss for all. We will generalize IRL algorithms to the multi-agent setting, where the ham and robot work side-by-side. Allow for some probability of human error. The uncertainty means more information from the subject is always better than choosing to avoid being switched off. To be certain at a future date means a false fixed objective has been set, a false conclusion made, false belief. Avoid prohibitions, instead making the robot want to defer to humans, like wanting to pay taxes. Rather than finding loopholes. Pragmatics in linguistics. Griceanism. Reinforcement learning with humans as reward signal leads to the system learning to control humans to maximize reward signal. Saying that alpha go wants to win is an oversimplification: winning was the reward in the reinforcement process, but desires and decisions are unknown. Discussions of robot desires must be much more nuanced. We are a complication in the world of AI. Issues: different humans, many humans (must make tradeoffs), satisfying the preferences of one person has implications for the wellbeing if others, loyal ai (liability becomes another loophole), sadistic people, utilitarian AI (consequentialism), how do we evaluate consequences that affect multiple people?, challenges to utilitarianism,  comparison of peoples’ feelings and utility (adding and subtracting subjective experiences), utility monsters (people who have greater desires or benefit from utility making them higs in the utility maximizing equation, everyone is a utility monster compared to rats), to be truly utilitarian the robot must lose some loyalty, nice nasty and envious humans, negative altruism, “justice” analysis, positional goods and zero-sum thinking, stupid emotional humans (all of us compared to the ideal, weare far from rational, acting in ways that are contraryto our true underlying preferences), we pursue near-term goals (the subroutine we are in currently), actions driven by emotion (can be good and rational, but also not), analyzing whether emotion is irrational or simply sadism, human preferences (uncertainty, computational limitations and error), incompletely specified choices, choosing between “future lives” (an impossibility in practice, but currently a choice) , mistaken choices because of uncertainty, experiencing self and remembering self (chooses experiences based on memory)(peak end memory), time and change, preference change vs preference update (in preference change, which or who’s preference do we choose?), preferences change with machine interaction, preferences for preference change.

Title: The men we need
Author: Brant hanson
Notes: A real man: women feel safe, a sense of security. The man as protector. It’s how women and babies look at him. Firefighters are attractive because they save people. When we prove we are willing to help, our character shines. Women don’t respect passive men, because they know they are meant for more, because a passive man is not a protector. They like men who show up, who know who they are. Adam was created to tend the garden, to look after it. Masculinity is about taking responsibility, being humble consistent dedicated keepers of the garden. What we need is the willingness to bring whatever resources we have, not superstrength, etc. The Man is like God, he looks after the needy and poor, the sick and afflicted. (Blessings, confidence in doing what you can, showing up). We can’t just do what we want, because others’ lives will be worse off because of our absence. They need good men. God called Adam when he hid, because Adam was the keeper of the garden, charged with responsibility. Actively do unto others, serve, help, defend, keep, care. A passive man is a threat to the woman, because he may be not up to the job of keeping her, of caring for her. Passive men are much more common than aggressive or “toxic” men. If you lived your life without commitment to anyone, what would be the point? How would you feel? Real women are challenging, but worth it, meaningful. Historically, we had no choice but to grow up. In our modern world, we can truly be useless, and never learn to grow up.  Be freaked out by the possibility that you might not become the man you were meant to be. Become that man. Sin is a rush of sweet, followed by bitter pain. A sweet fruit that becomes a pile of gravel.  Don’t fall for the swindle, the shortcut, the counterfeits. People are literally buying robots for connection, when the real thing, other humans, are all around them. The real female mind adds to, challenges, and refines us. Porn and fake sex are fakes. My sin is sin because it stops me becoming who I could be,preventing me from the kingdom of heaven.  Satan fishes with counterfeit exaggerated feed. None want the fake life, but they fall for it. Satan can only destroy or mock, replacing our meaning with meaninglessness.  Dopamine doesn’t give pleasure, it causes us to seek it, to look for pleasure. Dopamine issues are overseeking, raging fires, that are never satisfied. Overzealous longings we keep throwing gas and flammables on.  When you get over your dopamine addiction, you will realize the nonvirtual reality is just the reality you were made for. People around you should be safer because you are there. Are you looking out for others’ safety? Be aware of what’s happening around you (don’t be on your phone all the time with others or in public).  People need challenges. Males need threats, challenges, ways to help people. We need purpose.we are stewards. We are god’s hands, he expects us to start the car, wash dishes, work, garden, etc. He doesn’t do our work for us. What we do matters (it’s a wonderful life). If you need to do something, don’t assume it will get done. You are in your specific situation, others may not do it. You are there to help, do it. Others can’t do what you may. What we do has real consequences. The bystander effect: people do just stand by and watch. The treason is real. Your strength can be a threat to others, but your weakness can also be such. A woman will bet her future on you. Don’t invade your own garden. Our culture trains us to not tend our garden. Choose to be a keeper of your garden, a man among boys. It’s your job to shelter your family in appropriate ways. You are to create safety for the vulnerable. You must know your family well to be able to help and shelter them. You are here to shape character in your kids, not just skills. You can take anything too far. Most men don’t overprotect. Give them challenges, but filter what you give them to their age and temperament. If your kid has asthma, would you pump exhaust into their face? Would you show your child violent material and porn if they have a tendency or weakness toward such, pain with it? What are we creating for the people in our own home? A man creating danger in his own home is life altering, and extremely troublesome. Choose protection, care, mercy, forgiveness, and start the journey now. Set the tone, start planting these seeds. Be a kangaroo, hold the baby, give them what they need. Be a father to the fatherless, a defender of the weak. Babies can’t pay you back, much like many others. We do this because we love god. We love because he loves us, and it is our role to do so. Be ambitious about the right things. Reality does not bend to our beliefs. If we run into a wall, it hurts. Reality is what hits us when we are wrong. When we are ambitious about the wrong things, reality hits us hard. If you feel meaningless, it might be because you are investing your time in meaningless things.  Meaningless = things that don’t add value to anyone else's life. People rarely applaud the right things. Women like it, but you won't get praised. Everything we attend to is life-giving or ennui-giving.  People who are actively serving others don't struggle with meaninglessness. Invest in meaningless things and you will feel anger toward yourself, yielding irritation toward others, manifesting in odd ways. Am I making her feel more secure? Do my actions indicate that i’m willing to be here for her and the kids? Does she sense that i’m engaged with real life, willing to do what needs to be done for her. Women think risky guys are attractive until they think they are stupid. Men with ambition and not a lot of money are more attractive than lazy men with lots of money. Risk-taking becomes less attractive when she decides to trust you with her future. The initial risk-taking is attractive for your potential. She expects reliability once there is commitment, and for you to become that potential you, not keep swimming in dumb risks. Even dumb jobs are helping people. Work is a noble thing. See the meaning in your job, the bigger purpose and ways you are helping people. Bringing your all to what you are doing is a form of worship, serving God with all your might by serving others well. There is no mess-free work, or relationship. Men are called to be uncomfortable, to bring chaos into order, even though we favor comfort. Relationships require bravery. Rise to the occasion and take on the risk of relationships. Very few men feel like they are good at relationships.  If you can get your mind off yourself, you can make a difference in others’ lives, even if you feel dumb sometimes. No one else is in your exact situation. Wow that’s nice, amazing, attractive, and I don't need to have it. Play the game of contentment, to not covet. I have everything I need to do what I need today. I lack nothing I need. Allow yourself to lose. Ambition is not winning. Be ambitious about losing. It's OK to lose. Athletes are less despaired at loss than their fans. They care about being healthy, the climb, growth. The best ambition is becoming, and assurance in God. We need men who commit, even in a time of options.  We are used to being consumers, looking for upgrades.
