Commitment means closing doors in favor of a better one, and this is necessary in relationships. Jesus saw women as equals, as belonging. Jesus actively listened to women. It matters to the woman whether something matters to me if it matters to her. Jesus removes shame, rather than exposing and ridiculing it. Our culture treats women as consumables, loving ourselves for the feelings women give us, rather than loving the other human. We treat love as a symptom of our pleasure, not an altruistic choice. Don't live with a woman unless she is your wife. Sex outside of marriage is disintegrity, writing checks with your body that your soul can't keep. Protect them from you (be gentle). Use your words with care. We bless or curse people in every interaction, by what we do and say or communicate to them. The tongue is a sword. Build others up with your words. Kill your sinner self. On your deathbed, you will want relationships, not toys. When you have a family, tending the family garden is your priority. Guard, cultivate, and protect your kids while they are at home. Don't prioritize career and toys over them, don’t show them the wrong example. You can't do everything at once. For now, be the dad they need. Most scares about family life are wrong, except for the heartbreak when your kids move on and grow out of the home. What we pay attention to is everything. We don't struggle with lust, etc., when we are busy with other things. What you pay attention to affects others. A companion is anything you spend your time with. Hang out with fools, and you become more like a fool. Fools love to vent anger, don’t learn from mistakes, hate knowledge of God, can’t handle discipline, argue a lot, quick tempered, mock those who take repentance seriously, too busy telling you their opinions they don't want wisdom. You are very influenced by the company you keep, your companions, what has your attention. Ask God for wisdom. Wisdom is precious, because life is decisions, and reality hurts when we are wrong. Make the wise your companions. What kind of old man do you want to be? Every man over 40 is responsible for his own face. No one wants to experience hell. We are all becoming something, and need to course-correct continuously. You're not getting any younger, and we need you to be an other-centered man. Start now. Honorable men serve as foundations for their family, and may never be fully appreciated behind the grandeur of the building. Stop being needy by giving up traditional models of happiness. Pursue God, and gain persistent joy. Put your hope in God. Your need for admiration costs you admiration. We need men without any significant payoff in mind, who don't need approval. Do you know who you are as a son of God? No man steps in the same river twice. God changes people when they are humble, so ask God to help you be less needy.  If God be for us, who can be against us. Live without fear. God overcomes. Consider the lilies. Don't follow your heart, open your eyes.  Our natural desires and inclinations lead us astray. Take responsibility for your own spiritual life.  God wants your loyalty. Anger is not attractive. Don't be angry, take action. Anger is not a fruit of the spirit. Spirituality is not emotion. Jesus doesn’t talk about emotion. God is pleased by our obedience, not our feeling. If you're not emotional about your faith, don't worry about it. Turn your attention to God. Spirituality is not measured in goosebumps, but in action. It's possible you already know enough to be who you need to be. Put what Jesus said to do into practice. Live as he did. We sometimes prefer complexity and academics because we fear the action. “As long as I don't hurt anyone else” is a lie, pretending we are independent of others. Everything we do has consequences, ripples out. If you're not who you need to be, it hurts you, and hurts us. Do things when you don't feel like it. Have self control.  To gain more self control, change your circumstances and the people around you. Boldly ask God. We are Coworkers in the kingdom of god.

Title: Leadership and self-deception
Author: The arbinger institute
Notes: A book about why people are sometimes jerks. Self-deception keeps us from seeing and solving problems. When people are criticized, they rarely agree with the criticism. The bigger problem is when we can’t see that we have a problem. When we are stuck in our own experience, “stuck in the box”, in self-deception. There is a germ in organizations, the disease of self-deception. People care most about how others regard them, not what they do or say. How much you care is what matters most in influence. If you do things for you and not them, they know. In the box: our needs are primary, others second or trivial, we see others as objects, not people. We get in the box through self-betrayal, betraying our own sense of what we should do for others. Act contrary to what we feel we should do for another = self-betrayal. We can be hard on the problem, and still be out of the box and see someone as a human being. It’s not what we do necessarily, but how we do it. Justifications are self-betrayal. When we are in the box, we don’t see the truth, that people really are people like us, that their concerns are just as reasonable as ours. In our self-betrayal, we minimize our own faults, don’t see ourself clearly, don’t see others clearly, and increase the perceived catastrophy of our own concerns. Self-betrayl 1. When we act contrary to how we feel we should treat another human. 2. When we betray ourselves we see the world in a way that justifies our betrayal. 3. When we when I see the world in a self-justified way, my view of reality becomes distorted. 4. Our distortion means we are in the box. 5. over time, certain boxes become characteristic of me and I carry them with me. We inflate the others’ faults, our own virtues, the value of things that justify our self-betrayal, and blame. The box is a blame-space. In the box, our way of being is blaming. But are others truly to blame? Is that really the whole reality, seeing the world clearly? What really caused our irritation? Our self-betrayal. When I betray myself, I become self-deceived by entering the box. Before we betray ourselves, we see others simply as they are through our feelings of how to treat other humans. When we carry boxes or self-justifying images with us, we don’t have to have feelings of betray to be in the box, because we already are. We are already not seeing reality as it is, what is really true. Others’ problems don't excuse ours, that is a justification. Being in the box provokes others to be in the box. When we feel justified in mistreating others, they feel unjustly mistreated, and justify themselves. Our box needs us to justify ourselves, asking for more poor behavior from others so that we feel justified. What the box needs most is justification. In the box, we need others to be a problem. A disappointment, so we can justify our current pains, our self-betrayal. The box is destructive, creating the problems we blame others for. It's almost as if we collided to make trouble. When multiple people are in the box causing each other problems, we call it collusion. By being in the box, we Provoke the behaviors we hate most.  Our box (justification) is at odds with results and productivity. In the box, we focus on ourselves only, not true productivity. We can’t see this in the box, and Provoke other, and spread the propagation of lying to ourselves. One person in the box in an organization end up spreading the delight in others’ failures. It creates a culture of sick people. Don't be the doctor that spreads the germs. Self-betrayal creates self-deception, creating many other symptoms that we call people problems. How we get out of the box: when you want to be out of the box, you are already in that moment. What we worry about is how to stay out. How do we continue to see others as people? Don't try to change others, because we put ourselves in the box, not others. Don't cope with others (continuing to blame them). Don't leave others (the box goes with you). Don’t communicate (communicating in the box is unproductive). It's not the skill or technique, it's the way you do, the way you see. Your behavior? No, outward behavior in the box is just poorly-executed box behavior. “What do we do?” Is the wrong question. Question your own virtues. We never question our virtue when “in the blx”. How to stay out? Act on your impulses to treat them as humans. Do what you feel you should for others. This does not mean we do every good thing in the world, or add obligations to our life, but the people around us, those we encounter and connect with are people we must treat well. We cannot do the ideal at all times, but we must not justify ourselves, but instead know that we are doing the best we can, and still seeing others and things as they truly are. Allow others to be in the box without blaming them. You need to be a leader, to lead by example and not coercion. Be free of self-betrayal to be a leader people want to follow and become like.  Remember that we don't need blame, because we all contribute. Refuse to blame others, and instead accept responsibility. Others will be happier to work with you. Remember: learn how you can be more helpful to others, when you are in the box, you can't focus on results, your influence and success depend on being out of the box, you get out of the box by ceasing to resist other people, Don't try to be perfect but try to be better, use the principles in your life, don't look for others’ boxes, don't accuse others of being in the box, don’t deny your being in the box, focus on what you can do right to help, worry about whether you are helping others. Companies fail for the same reasons families do. We don't know those around us until we leave the box and join them. As far as I am concerned, the problem is me. We know about self-deception because we see it in others, but we are usually not skilled at seeing it in ourselves. Outward mindset = out of the box.  Change in an organization starts with the leader, as they accept responsibility.

Title: The almanac of naval ravikant
Author: Eric Jorgenson, Tim ferriss
Notes: If you can’t explain it to a child, you don’t understand. Explaining simply and being a clear thinker is better than being called “smart”. Great ideas come with empty time, when you are bored. A contrarian resists pressure to conform. Shed your identity to see reality. Pain forces you to experience reality. Avoid identity labels. There are no permanent solutions. Relaxation is who you are, tension is who you think you should be. You are not your actions or profession, these are habits. Being green means I can say what I say and think what I think. You are the easiest person to fool, don’t lie to yourself. Get a solid foundation in what you start reading, because it builds your view of the world: stick to math and science as guiding rods. Start with the classics, the originals, in whatever you are interested. Careful what you read, all thoughts are like songs you can’t get out of your head.

Title: Effortless
Author: Greg mckeown
Notes: Working harder is not always the answer. When you can’t try harder, it’s time to find a different path. Burnout is not a badge of honor. What if there are too many big rocks, they don’t fit in the container of time? Not everything has to be so hard. Essentialism is about doing the right things. Effortless is about doing them the right way. Making a free-throw is effortless action. Nothing but net, at peace, comfortable, fully here. Most important part of the process? Don’t overthink it. Get into flowstate. Computers slow when cluttered. When overwhelmed with information, our brain chooses to prioritize high priority emotions: fear, anger, etc. Removing burdens let's us see more clearly, be more energized, be in the moment. Our culture has defaulted to seeing important things as hard, and wrong things as easy. Hard = good, easy = bad. Challenge this thinking. We have a bias for path of least resistance. What if this essential project could be made easy? Puritanism embraced the hard and distrusted the easy. We seem to have inherited this view. Trying too hard makes it harder to achieve. Overachieving ≠ overworking. Effortless inversion: invert the question, what if this could be easy? What if all those “required steps” are not truly required? Try without trying. Those whonsucceed think that the essential tasks can be the most effortless. Anything can be effortless, but not everything. Find an indirect approach, simplify, a better way? Can you push something downhill, not uphill? Business strategy: Solve the easiest problem. Warren buffet strategy: look for no-brainer businesses to invest in, easy to run, long-term advantage, not difficult projects. “I look around for 1-foot bars that I can step over”. What’s the simplest way to achieve this result? Shed the assumption that the easier path has to be the inferior path. What if this could be fun? Essential work can be fun once we put aside the puritan notion that anything worth doing must entail backbreaking effort. Don’t separate all work from play. Lag indicators: you experience reward long after the action took place. Decrease the lag time by enjoying the activity, pairing the activity with the reward. Call people from your hot tub. How can you make it fun? Make the steps of the process bearable, or even fun. Don’t reward yourself after, reward during the process. Create building blocks of joy: like productive play with Legos, create order from chaos, make a task you dislike a ritual you look forward to. Rituals are about how you do something, like Marie Kondo’s ritual of letting things go when tidying. Rituals are habits with a soul, bringing us back to ourselves, a natural playful state. Release: the power of letting go. Do you have outdated goals living rent-free in your mind? They act like unnecessary background apps. Focus on what you are thankful for during your misfortune: a “have” state, a openness. Positive emotions creat upward spirals, open us to creativity and new ideas. Focus on what you have, to get what you lack. Negative emotions narrow our mindset. Set the positive emotions, gratitude, into motion, the system into motion. Eventually it will become effortless, as it gets easier and easier.  Rule: after you complain, state one thing you are thankful for. “What job have I hired this grudge to do?” Your grudge is not fulfilling the job request, hire another habit or activity. Accept people for who they are, that they are who they showed themselves to be, that you don’t need to expect them to change or do more than they offered before. Forgive and let go of their hurt. Rest: necessary. Dedicate mornings to essential work, break down that work into 3 sessions of no more than 90 mins each, take a short break (10-15 mins) between sessions to rest and recover. Do not do more today than you can completely recover from today. Same for a week. Rest is a responsibility. We get less sleep than people used to. Perception habits, attentional muscles. To be in the effortless state is to be aware, present, attentive. Turn toward: Receive the bid for attention and return the served tennis ball. Be present with people. Quakers’ clearness committee: focus person shares a dilemma met by silence, then committee asks a few clarifying questions, reflect or repeat back what they heard, but not give advice or opinions or judgment. They let people amplify their inner voice, letting them discover what is right. Prepare your space, rest your body, relax your mind, release your heart (forgive), breath in gratitude. The effortless state: what if this could be easy? What if this could be fun? What job have I hired this grudge to do? Sleep, recover,  and take a nap. Clear clutter, be present, ignore the irrelevant. More effort doesn’t always work. Pushing harder can decrease output. Wu wei: Effortless action. Define what “done” looks like. Stop at “done”. Swedish death cleaning: clean while you are alive, to avoid having your relatives do it when you are died. Define what “done” looks like for your life. The “now” we experience is only 2.5 seconds. That is where the change in our life happens. Take the first step in those 2.5 seconds. The simplest step is the one you don’t take, and it's easier to take no step. The courage to be rubbish. Everything starts out ugly, rubbish, or flawed, with mistakes. The faster you make mistakes, the faster you progress. Make failure as cheap/inexpensive as possible. Learn the easy way before the hard way. Let go of doing things perfectly. Have an error rate of 10-20%. Too perfect is imperfect. Writing is power. Even rubbish words are better than a blank page. Start small and begin making rubbish. A one-time impact is linear-action. Linear results are limited. Residual results are infinite in rewards. Perpetual results: effortless wealth. Use levers: learning, teaching, automating, trusting (hire, unify), preventing (strike problem at roots). These can also create bad results, but use them for effortless power. Learn: leverage the best of what others know. Easy fast solutions are tempting, but principles are the key. Seek principles. Principles are trunks and roots of trees. First principles are what you can keep, as there is too much detail in the world to memorize. The older a book is, the higher the likelihood it will survive into the future. Distill ideas into their essentials. Teach: harness others’ power. Teach people to teach. Simply the most important messages. Go for the straightforward message that can be easily understood. Automate: high tech = low effort. Anything that solves a problem with minimal human effort. Washing machines, thermostat, etc. What is a problem that irritates me frequently? What is the total cost of managing that over several years? What is the next step i can take immediately towards solving it? Hack at the roots. It’s never too early. Measure twice, cut once.  For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

Title: You are not so smart
Author: David McRaney
Notes:
Just about every physical object you encounter triggers a blitz of associations throughout your mind. You construct reality from minute to minute with memories and emotions orbiting your sensations and cognition. (You are walking memory, and make meaning based on perception and the relevant memory and emotion). Smell is a great example of this. We like and dislike certain smells, but many smells are neutral, and only perceived one way or another based on previous experience, or memory and emotion, what we think we remember. This sort of priming or influence with our action or perception works best when we are on autopilot and not consciously trying to introspect. Your brain hates ambiguity, and is willing to take shortcuts to remove it. It uses what is available. If pattern recognition fails, your create patterns of your own. You also chunk perceptions all the time to reduce complexity. Written language is valuable because it escapes the rational mind and its limits. The emotional brain is better at breakdancing, somersaults and singing because these actions require too many steps and variables for the rational mind to handle. You hand these tasks over to the adaptive unconscious. Animals with small cerebral cortices, or none, are mostly on autopilot because their emotional brain runs the show. We mistakenly believe our rational mind is in control, oblivious to the influence of our subconscious. We are comfortable with top-down control (hugging and then feeling endorphins),  but find bottom-up control odd or uncomfortable (simply observing a briefcase makes you act more greedily than you otherwise would, taking advise from the hidden advisors of emotion and subconscious). From every corner of the modern world, advertisers are launching attacks on your unconscious to prime your behavior to be more favorable to their bottom lines. We believe the things around us don’t effect us. Much of what you think, feel, do, believe is, and will continue to be, nudged by primes from words, colors, objects, smells, personalities, etc. That are infused with meaning via your life or cultural experience. Make plans in advance to be primed, such as making a grocery list that keeps you on track and avoids autopilot roaming the store. You can't prime yourself directly, but you can create environments conducive to mental states you desire. Choose to be an agent and prime others: smile, dress appropriately, etc. When you least expect it, your environment will nudge you. Your brain fills in gaps, blindspots in your memory, reason, and perception. The details are missing, but the big picture persists, which is often a lie  to a degree, because the left and right brain send signals to each other and undoubtedly miscommunicate.. they often must invent reasons for why they receive a signal, and without the connections biologically between the two brain halves, they would make up explanations or be at a loss for reason all of the time. The left hemisphere often leads the dance because it deals with talking. You are a confabulatory creature by nature, and create reasons for the causes and motivations in your life. Over time, this becomes your idea of who you are and your place in the world, or your “self”. Your sense of self is partly your mirror neurons, which fire when you see others experience things, but also when you act, as if part of your brain observes you from the outside. “You” is a story you tell yourself, a confabulation that without which you could not function. When you recall the past, you create it on the spot, using part memory and part fantasy to recreate memory which you believe fully. We don't believe our daydreams usually. But believe our inaccurate recollection. We are unaware of how our mind works, of how we come to decisions and feelings. We merely make up stories. Ask yourself to recall your mother’s maiden name, and you will have no clue how you truly remembered it, you just “thought”. In many ways, you only report on what your mind has 
already produced, instead of directing the production. Phenomenology. Consciousness and recollection of it are separate, but we often think of them as one. Heterophenomenology. Take your own perception with a grain of salt. We seldom simply say we don't know why we do what we do. We almost always 
find a way to justify our actions in some way. Who you think you are is like a movie based on true events. It's embellished, but tye bigger picture is there and still worth hearing about. You can't ever know the objective truth, but that's OK. Confirmation bias: seeing the world through a filter, partly due to seeing top-of-mind topics everywhere. People like to be told what they already know, to watch for confirmation, not information. People think they crave news, but they really crave olds. You want to be right about how you see the world, so you seek to confirm your views, not contradict them. Even recalling memory falls prey to this, meaning memory can be rewritten unconsciously to fit our biases. Remember there's always someone willing to sell an audience looking for validation. Are you part of that audience? Hindsight bias: we assume we new or believed it all along. When you learn something new, you quickly redact your past so you can feel the comfort of always being right. What we usually think of as common sense, usually isn't. It's more likely hindsight bias reconstructing our past views to fit current settings. We likewise delete old info about ourselves when we change, because we don't need the clutter anymore. We remember ourselves as being more accurately inside with current circumstances, our past predictions as more accurate, our past follies as less problematic, than they are. Much like the availability heuristic, we tend to prioritize what is in front of us, and see the world through that lense, seeing it as more prevalent than it is, because that is what is there. We truly think reality is what is currently attended to, and rewrite the past to fit the present. We all think we were never wrong.  The Texas sharpshooter fallacy: you tend to ignore random chance when results seem meaningful or when you want random events to have meaningful cause. With meaning you overlook randomness, but meaning is a human construction. we paint a bull’s-eye over an already tattered cluster of bulletholes, making artificial order of natural chaos. Reality TV, news, etc., do this all day. They draw a target over a cluster of randomness to make a point, a story, to fit their agenda. Essentially, the sharpshooter fallacy is a way to find a target, an enemy, to deal with the anxiety of being at the whim of chance, and the way is to ignore Confounding variables and the bigger picture of random chance. It is humans finding meaning after the fact, after the numbers have been crunched, ignoring all the times the ball missed the basket, or the church was torn by a tornado, or the casino luck didn't pan out. Only the need for meaning changes how you feel about what you see. Creating this false order helped our ancestors survive.  We see patterns everywhere, but some of them are merely chance.  Procrastination: you have time-inconsistent preferences. You will plan for fruit, but take the cake instead on the actual day. In the moment, you go for what taste good, present-bias (unable to grasp that what you want will change over time, and what you want now isn’t what you’ll want later). Your will succumbs to death by a thousand cuts, as you make poor present choices over and over. (Thus, often, action precedes desire). You’re not a bad manager, you're a bad tactician inside your brain’s war. The marshmallow kids tricked themselves into getting what they would want later. They looked at the wall, tapped their feet, instead of staring at the marshmallow. Thinking about thinking, is the key. “Want” never goes away. Hyperbolic discounting. Believe that you will procrastinate or struggle, or else you never develop a strategy to cope with it and become overly idealistic about your capabikities. Now-you needs to convince future-you to make a different choice rather than giving in to old habit or temptation. This is why buying only good food is a better health plan then other alternatives, etc. Future-you has to deal with that choice in the fiture, but not make it initially. Normalcy bias: we tend to believe that things are normal, even in emergency. We will assume that it is someone else's problem. That we are not in danger. To the point we calm others down so we don't have to feel panicked, to reassure ourselves that things are still normal. Pretending evrryth8ng will continue to be fine Freeze state almost, and some enter freeze state. Those who act and survive are those who prepared, thought ahead, and rehearsed in their mind what they would do or practiced their strategy. Cognition, perception, comprehension, decision, implementation, and then movement. N9rmalcy bias is not freeze state. It is self-soothing. It is seeing the world as if nothing bad happened so you can feel safe. Refusing to beleive that terrible events will include you. Denial of yourself as part of the unnatural or nonnormal. In disaster you feel the need to feel safe. Survivors of 9 11 walked out of the building leisurely as if nothing wrong was happening, calling loved ones and gathering belongings on their way. You will cling to normalcy, to what you know. Then you will mine others for information. First you will interpret based on what you know, likely severely underestimate yhe threat, seek information from those you trust, then those around you, then contact family, then prepare to evacuate . Introspection: origin of your feelings is not clear to you, even though you make up reasons and justifications.

Title: Don't believe everything you think
Author: Joseph Nguyen
Notes:
Truth is simple, exeprienced. Two arrows: the first is our experience, the second our reaction. We live through our own perception of the world. We therefore live in a world of thought, not reality. Our thought creates our “reality”. True reality is the objective present without attached meaning. Any meaning or thinking we give something is self-created and our choice. It’s not events, but our interpretation of them that causes us good or bad feelings. Our thinking about events is the cause of our pain. If external events were solely responsible for our level of happiness, we would be happy a lot more often and less often than we would assume. You wouldn’t be sad in your room alone, sad while watching TV, sad while spending time with other people, sad at the gym, etc. Internal influences are a much bigger part of the picture than we assume. Must a particular experience lead to suffering? Would everyone in that situation feel the same about it? No. How would you feel if you didn’t think that you hate____? Without our usual thinking, our experience is completely altered. The root cause of our suffering is our own thinking. By changing our thinking, we change our reality. Our experience is not inevitable. We are one thought away from transforming our life experience. Serenity is the following: event + no thinking = reality/peace. Without my reaction, nothing has the power to make me angry. What really causes you pain? You do. True freedom is the ability to unattached to whatever happens in the mind. What happens around us is like an empty boat floating toward us. There is no one to blame, no one steering the “disturbance”. The mind evolved to think, to keep us alive. Much of this survival thinking costs us peace and happiness. We navigate the modern world with a mind programmed with primitive fears. You are not a product of your environment, but a co-creator with it. Thoughts = neutral observations, insights, or intuitive promptings that enter our mind. Thinking = our judgment or opinion we have about our thoughts. Thought is a noun, thinking a verb (something we do). Thoughts are intrinsically neutral, but our thinking takes us on an emotional journey with thoughts. The usefulness of thinking is an illusion that causes us to experience negative, unwanted emotions. Thoughts create, thinking often destroys. The idea is to sit with the spontaneous thoughts springing up, as this is creativity. [Does it not matter what question prompts our thoughts though?]. Our emotions tell us whether we are experiencing thought, or thinking (ruminating). As you begin thinking, you’ll feel a cascade of negative emotions. Our natural state is joy: love, compassion, healing.  Our goal is not to stop feeling negative emotions, because emotions are signals. The goal is to decrease the amount of time it takes us to regulate and return to a state of peace. While positive thought can lead to positive emotion, it is not required. You don’t feel happy only when you have positive thoughts, hero when you think positively (which would be a chore if that were the case). Positive emotion is solely the byproduct of being fully in the present moment and connected to life, rather than thinking about it. Our natural state of being is joy, love, and peace. Children exemplify this, naturally being in a state of openness, curiosity, laughter, wonder. The times you are most stressed, you are thinking most. The times you are most calm and at peace, you are thinking least. It’s not the content of our thinking, but that, or how much, we are thinking. Thinking takes us away from the present into the past or future. You do not have to try to be present or thinking positively. More often, the solution is removal, not addition.  [As we get older, we learn to think and have much more ro think about. We spend less time experiencing and more time thinking, of necessity to some degree, but also as a learned habit]. Don’t seek the external to feel inside, because feelings are created within. We don’t therefore have to do anything to minimize our consuming thought. Simply become aware and let go. A process of flow, not force. Stop resisting and avoiding. What we resist persists. What we accept and let be will leave inevitably.  If we let our mind sit  without fighting  it, the dirt settles to the bottom. Acknowledge your thinking and give it the space to pass without judgment, and slowly the mind will clear again.  To stop thinking: PAUSE. Pause, take some deep breaths. Ask, asking yourself “does this thinking help me feel the way i want to?”. Understand, that you have the choice to let go of your thinking. Say, repeating to yourself “thinking is the root cause of suffering”.  Experience feeling your emotions fully.  Don’t we need thinking to survive in the world when you enter flow state, how much thinking is going on? It’s minimal to none. Our flow is not about thinking or “judgment”, it is a natural state of intuition and creativity and presence. The thoughts that come are neutral, constructive, creative. We really do do our best work in a state of non-thinking.  Athletes enter “the zone” in peak performance. They don’t think, they act on instinct based on former practice and formed habits in the subconscious.  We may attribute our flow to a particular activity when we are in non-thinking. This creates a false belief that that activity alone is when we can feel flow or fully present. We can be in flow anytime we are in the present moment.  The divine is in the present only. “I am”, not i was, or i will be. You cannot think your way into flow or love. They are an occurance, a byproduct, of the present.  As with thoughts and thinking, where our goals and dreams come from will determine whether they make us suffer or how we feel pursuing them. Do they come from our higher self, or are they the product of our ego or “thinking”. Two sources: goals created out of inspiration, and goals created out of desperation. Desperation goals create 
feelings of immense scarcity and urgency , imposter syndrome, self doubt, being short on time, and even if we accomplish  the goal, shortly after we nginue ti feel discontented, lacking, and compare ourselves to others. These desperation goals are means goals, not “ends” goals. They aim to get something from the goal, to let something external fix the internal. Example: become famous, to be valued. Unless we fix the underlying feeling of not being valued  or not being good enough, the external goal will never change how you feel. Desperation goals leave us feeling emptier than before, so we set even bigger goals, etc. Inspiration goals: creating because we feel moved, inspired, expansive. It feels like a calling, not obligation. We feel like a force of life comes from within , pulled instead of forced, from a place of abundance. What did you dream of doing when you were a kid we naturally have inspiration goals all the time as adults. This creation is an overflowing of love and joy for life. We create because we want to. This feeling of inspiration comes through us from something greater than ourselves. We call it “divine inspiration”, because these ideas of what we want to create seem far greater   bigger than we could come up with on our own. In this state, we feel whole, complete, unconditional love, etc. Most of us suppress this divine inspiration with thinking, that creates self-doubt. Loving a life of non-thinking means we create goals out of inspiration not desperation. How do we know which is which? They look similar, but are different under the surface. Goals and dreams created from thought are of inspiration, while goals and dreams from thinking are of desperation. Desperation goals usually have conditional happiness only via achievemen, rooted in fear. Goals of inspiration comes from what you value. Most of the time, inspiration goals will lead to greater happiness, and may achieve some of the desperation goals’ aims, but there are no good or bad goals. We still need financial goals, and to live and survive.   The same aims can be based on inspiration or desperation. Ask yourself “what does ____ (making money)  give me or allow me to do that I value most?”. We don’therefore drop everything to achieve our inspiration goals. Think “everyday” rather than a time quota or how much. What are you doing everyday to support your goal of creating a happy family? It’s not about if, but how you can make it happen. As with thoughts, inspiration dreams and goals just pop up and come naturally. We don’therefore need to do extra work to find these aspirations. If I had infinite money, no fear, and didn't need to receive any recognition, what would I do or create? We learned to stuff this inspiration. A mind without thinking has no limits. Good and bad: a piano has no bad keys. Only in the context of a piece do certain keys sound unlikeable or unnatural. There is not one correct path. Don’t label paths as wrong or right, stay open to opportunities. There are no wrong spots to pause on a mountain. Instead of l[king for right or wrong, look for truth without judgment. Look for universal truths. These truths are not subjective, and are rarely at the extremes.  A wise person is always unlearning.  Intuition leads us to who we want to be. Your intuition is usually the choice that makes you feel a tinge of fear because it requires you to step into the unknown to create a new reality rather than stay in your familiar one.  Nothing that grows can stay the same, especially your. We live in an illusion of certainty. Most of what we have can be taken away in a moment. We know the only constant is change, yet we spend our energy fighting it. Relax into uncertainty. Accept things as they are, instead of how you think they should be. Trust you will be ok no matter what happens. We can’therefore control all that happens, but we can choose our response. Our job is determining what we want, not necessarily how we get it. Delegate the “hiw” to your intuition because there are infinite ways to get what you want. We will be given the next step. The pathis only revealed as we begin walking. Fwad stops us from heeding our intuition. Following your intuition may sometimes make others uncomfortable because they are not ready for you to change. Don’t sacrifice your peace for their temporary peace. Are you making decisions to feel safe, or to feel free?  If your mind is full of old ideas, you won’t have space for new thoughts. New thoughts are necessary for the change you seek.  Asking questions that challenge our current thinking is one of the best ways to create space in our minds. For peak performance athletes, intense rest happens after intense training. Strength is created in the rest. Nietzsche took walks for mental space, Einstein played violin. Space is like rest, we need it for our new ideas and mental wellness. What we do not question controls us, what we question frees us. But am I just lazy? Nonthinking is our most productive state. Slow down. If you’ve been living life in fight or flight, you may be uncomfortable without those feelings. This is a growing pain that will dissipate. Practicing nonthinkin does not mean avoiding reality, but accepting reality as it really is rather than what we think it should be. It is a space of nonjudgment.using thoughts instead of thinking. Channel your energy into your goals of inspiration instead of thinking. Create an activation ritual or a morning routine that helps you get into flow or nonthinking. An object in motion will stay in motion. To the person who is at peace with the feeling of fear, the whole universe yields. Unconditional love. Courage is the presence of love in the midst of fear. Others may critique or tell us we are not enough, they are simply caught up in their own thinking. You don’t have to listen. Live via your intuition. You already have all you want or could dream of within you. The only thing stopping us from doing what we truly desire is our fear. Question what it is that you are truly afraid of. Anxiety is an illusion designed to keep us in our comfort zone: nothing more.

Title: Real artists don’t starve
Author: Jeff goins
Notes: Take small leaps, small steps. Don’t quit your job, just do something everyday, make small meaningful bits of art, parts of your craft. We are either becoming more of our true selves, or something else. Life is not static. Always strive to reinvent yourself. Let go of the starving artist mentality. The most famous artists did not starve. The ancient masters and artists were praised for copying the work of their predecessors, a sign of their ability. Copying other’s work is being a student. After we are students, we can be masters and then steal like an artist, making something original from those we borrow from. We find our voice by mimicking the voice of others. You are not an artist because you steal, you steal because you are an artist (you’re not a copycat, you internalize a craft, and your style and voice emerges). Cite your sources. Don’t vet lost in the pursuit of originality. You know you’ve done your job, when you are no longer the thief, but the one being stolen and borrowed from. Apprentice under a master. Apprentice yourself. Get a mentor and be humble enough to learn, but tenacious enough to get their acceptance. Be flexible on the details, but stubborn on the vision. Don’t be insane, doing the same thing over and over again. You can't succeed on your own. Iterate and learn from others. Often success is not skill but tenacity and perseverance. You need a patron. Good art is subjective. We need people to tell us and others what is good or not. You need a patron or influener that makes things happen. You need an audience of one fist, and this makes success all the more likely. The patron must vouch for your success. You need an advocate that believes in your vision. You need to cultivate your patron. Where are these patrons, tastemakers? Closer than you think. All around us, rhere are patrons that are willing to support us. We must be teachable. Influencers love to invest in others, so make it easy on them. Be willing to learn. Show them you are applying their advice. Make good things, make it convenient and easy to connect with a patron, and be willing to learn from them. Use your day job as a patron, as a means to an end, a support for your art. Learn skills from your job, let it fund your craft. Pursuing patrons (an evangelist): seek out masters, all around you. Patrons need artists to support. Genius is a place, not a person. A network. If they don’t let you join, start yoir own creative space, and others that appreciate you will join you. Embrace your place. Put yourself where creativity is happening. Earn the attention of those already seen by serving them. Artist = visionary that brings people together. You must be findable. Practice in public. Always work for something. If you find yourself holding a grudge against your clients, or upset with them. Charge more for your work. Don’t make a habit of working for free. Stand up for yourself. Be your own patron.

Title: The architecture of happiness
Author: Alain de botton
Notes: Every building speaks, has a message. It speaks of longing for the past or visions of the future. Buildings talk to us, about the values we want to live by. Architecture is never neutral, simply beautiful, or simply functional, but always tells us something. If a form is attractive to us, it may because we interpret it as familial, as a mother’s thigh or a baby’s chin/arm, as human. Small visual changes can speak volumes about our psychological state, thus different arches suggest different feelings or characters. We sense in differences on human behavior a difference in feeling or interaction, such as contempt vs concern, etc. We can’t view objects without relating them to historical feelings or experiences or what we see their history. Our unconscious associative powers make these connections, though they are arbitrary much of the time. Many times, we dislike something simply because it reminds us of something else we disliked, etc. Genuinely beautiful objects may withstand our positive or negative projections and stand the test of time beyond our arbitrary associations. In a way, beauty is the promise of happiness. There are as many styles of beauty as there are happiness. The more we lose nature in our life, the more we seek it in our art, architecture, poetry, etc. The diversity of tastes in beauty is natural, as diversify of beauties is natural, and each serves a purpose for us. We need grandeur, but also coziness. If beauty could be made into laws, we would have created the most beautiful cities again out of raw material, easily. Social beliefs are like beliefs about beauty. We put names to characteristics, but irrationally come to these conclusions, borrow them from philosophers, or come to value them in haphazard ways. Yet there are some basic means we describe as beauty: order (surrender of individual to the greatness of the whole,  numbers, regularity/simplicity/predictability, coherence, consistency), order with complexity/intricacies . Contrast. elegance: There is beauty in durability and strength, paired with modesty.  Coherence:  buildings are choirs, not individual voices. The harmonize with their parts, and coherence with their settings (there is no Holland naturally in japan). Bad architecture is a failure in psychology and design. Create buildings that solve needs we didn’t know we had. Architecture lacking congeniality will arouse irritation, which people may not be able to describe, and may ascribe to mysticism beliefs or religious notions for lack of knowing how to express them. We can mold circumstances for the better, and the same with buildings done poorly. Our visual and emotional faculties need direction and guidance on what to focus on: we call it culture. Japanese have a different aesthetic taste in beauty, formed by their authors, artists, and philosophers. We often repress our preferences that do not fit culture, until someone is willing to hear it.

Title: Endure
Author: Alexander Hutchinson
Notes: We can’t help but pace ourselves, guess how much we have left in us. Our endurance is not defined by how much we actually have left in us, but how much further we THINK or believe we can go. Our head can hold us back or help us forward. Perception of limits is what keeps us back or pushes us forward to ultimate endurance. Being able to keep our mind from wandering, like the marshmallow test, impulse inhibition matters. Response inhibition seems to be a finite resource that depletes when used heavily and restores later. These skills are likely both born, and made through practice. Mental endurance is a key part of physical endurance. There are physical needs involved, but sports psychology is a huge factor.  Pain: without pain, you can’t manage or pace yourself. You need some pain. Many top athletes can endure a lot of pain, and may even enjoy it. You run your shin after bumping it to cause endorphins that crowd out the painful feelings. Stress can increase tolerance to pain, by using endocannabinoids or such. Muscle:
