Title: Off the clock
Author: Laura vanderkam
Notes: People most satisfied with their time are intentional with their time, cut out unnecessary things, make plans, spend time present during leisure, know that good enough is good enough, and focus on people—knowing that people are worth the time. People who feel abundant with their time can feel off the clock during paid work. You can feel relaxed during plans you have made. Time is fluid, you are in control. People who do more meditative and reflective activity feel they have more time. Time is not to be feared. How to feel time abundant: Tend your garden, make life memorable, don’t fill time, linger, invest in your happiness, let it go, people are a good use of time. Leave time open on your calendar, and when needed activities must be rescheduled, you can move items to those times if needed. Track your time, be Mindful of your hours, and you will see the weeds and issues with the soil, etc. Mind your garden, and you will have more choices and time to decide. We tend to exaggerate the time we spend on activities. We think we spend more time than we do, and often spend more time on mindless activities than we think we do. Memory is not like a filing cabinet. The past is as much defined by how you interact with it now as it is by what happened. The richness of the relationship relies on the treasuring of the past. We feel like time is ours when we remember. More memories means more time. We feel like time is slipping by when we don’t remember what happened. Routines are comfortable because we don’t have to think about them, they are utilitarian. Your thousands or drives in the car can be consolidated into one drive in memory. Other parts of life are different. When we are young, all is new. Time passes the same, but when we get older, things seem familiar and monotonous, and thus time passes more quickly to us. The memory that stands out to us as adults is about novelty and unique experiences and change. Craft a mindset of adventure to create interest and memory in the most boring days. You don’t want every week or day to be long and novelty. Find a balance between routine and novelty. Intentionally plan time for adventure and new experiences. Three selves: anticipating, experiencing, and remembering selves. In planning and executing new experiences, we need to priorities the anticipating and remembering self. The experiencing self must be put in the background. The experiencing self has to endure tiredness or the pains of new experiences or using energy. Remind yourself: “all times pass”. The experiencing self is in the present, unsure of the good that will come from new experiences and effort, rather than liesure in the present all the time. Find ways to recall memories: ask people to tell stories, do something with your photos, journal, etc. Make some time to dwell in the past. Dwelling in the past requires compassiom and forgiveness for your past selves. Be a good steward of your time. But leave open space. Deckutter your calendar though it’s undoable, what if you only had things on your calendar that sparked joy? Let time flow like water, instead of having lots of meetings and space filled for no other reason than to fill space. If you make plans for things you like, it’s easier to say no to things people ask you to do that you don’t like. Declare a Jubilee for time, or amnesty where you will Marie Kondo  your calendar. Get rid of unintentional traditions. All things end. Be careful with the words yes to the future you’self commitments. Ask “would I do this tomorrow?” if not, maybe you won't do it in October. People won't notice most of the things you do. They are too busy in their own world, being busy for their own work or boss. Big changes in circumstances are often why we declare amnesties, though some people impressively decide on their own. When life changes, the things that are not crucial simply have to go out of necessity. Work that doesn't get you to the life you want is still wasted time. Create time dovidends: things that creates more time in the future, like hiring an apprentice or assistant, learning habits for your future self, teaching your kids to cook, designating spots for keys, phones, etc. If you will do something again, ask if there is anything you can do to make it easier or quicker the next time. Be disciplined, don’t interrupt your time with checking your phone and other things like emails. Be more mindful and present, and don't fill your time with easy scrolling or other entertainment. Do things in the real world that you love. Linger: the opposite of rushing, giving things the time they deserve. If you are enjoying something, stick with it. This can be part of your adventure, or creating new experiences. Tell yourself “there is nothing wrong”. If you have nothing else to do, just linger, lean-in, and be present. Enjoying the present isn't easy. Be where you need to be with enough time to relax and prepare. Late people tend to be wildly optimistic, and people pleasers. To avoid feeling frantic about time, stop being late. Observe how long things take. Just add in extra time if you can't estimate the time. For example, arrive 15 mins before the expected time. Savor the present, hold yourself right where you are. Take in your surroundings. Record the experience and savor it, with your mind and senses, creating more memory. Share the event with others, tell others about it in the moment, etc. Kill-joys: it could have been better, thinking about other places or times, etc. Cognitive distortions, and such. Appreciate the ordinary good in the moment.  Invest in your happiness: when people say they want more time, they often mean they want more time doing things they love, or memories. We want to spend time doing things that make us happy. Exercise, reflective activities, and interacting with people. Can money buy happiness? Happiness can be measured in many ways moment by moment happiness is often driving our moods. Money spent to reduce time on things you don't enjoy, and increase enjoyable time, is money well-spent. For most treats, fear of hedonism is misplaced. Invest in your happiness by making use of grown-up goodies (that pen that makes writing pleasurable, etc.) Pay yourself first, woth money, but also time. Look at your mornings. Do you invest time in reflection, exercise, praying, Journaling?  If you don't invest in yourself, time will fill that space. Time is elastic. If you do what you love, you still get other things done in the time alotted them. Not all life will be fun. Suffering is part of life, and can be meaningful if we change from it. We can also find moments of beauty and joy amid the suffering, and manage our time well to do things that bring us joy amid the suffering. This too shall pass. The mentality and perspective we choose makes a huge difference. Be grateful for the journey. Let go of unreasonable expectations. You can't envy, be perfectiknistic, etc. Be a satisficer, knowing that “the best” does not exist. Good enough is good enough. Love is finding someone who is willing to settle for you. Everyone marries the wrong person and then commits to make it work. We simply choose people who are compatible and of good character, and then make it work. Don’t be a maximizer, stop worrying. Just pick something thar a friend mentioned or somewhere you’ve chosen before. Pick a simple choice, and then have a simple alternative. Waste less time on maximizing, and then have more time for yourself and people you love. Focus on process goals (inputs, and habit goals, rather than outcomes). Small things done repeatedly, add up. Low expectations but consistency. Love is acceptance. People must be taken as they are. Let go of expectations for people. Making time for people can increase your time. They help you feel less stressed, offer connections, and give you satisfaction in your life, making you more productive. During the busy years, we are tempted to put people last. Be intentional about people, instead of spending time on things like TV and games, etc. Treat relationships woth same intentionality as work. Each quarter should have a career goal, personal goal, and relational goal. If your calendar is looking bare, that can be a nudge to reach out to people. There are people you naturally see often during your week, and people you see rarely. Plan ahead for solo activities with people/family. You can wait for opportunities, or you can plan for them, because life rarely lines up opportunities. Time is all about intentionality. You rarely show up to work without a plan or intention. Do the same for your home life, family, and friends. A good leader asks people to do things only he would do, building loyalty. Build loyalty by spending relaxed time together. In-the-hall chats can be a vital part of the job. Professional success still stems from relationships. Going to happy hour one night is balanced, you have all the other nights to be at home. Listen to people. Everyone likes to feel heard. Give chitchat at the beginning of a meeting. Networking is nothing more than building authentic relationships with people you are interested in getting to know and spending time with. Reach out to someone every day. Make a list of 5 people every Friday, and then reach out during the week. Start with compliment, offer advice if appropriate, ask for ideas, connect, etc. Most people could spare more friend time in their life. Go big with events, they are better excuses for meeting up or connecting. Make standing dates for smaller groups who are local. This makes easy recurring appointments predictable and on the calendar. Meet up with friends on business trips, collaborate with peers who can work with you. Be selective about people. Not all relationships will last. Some people will never deepen you spirit. In any community, there are always newcomers and those willing to welcome, and those who are not. Visit old acquaintances and friends. The happiness of your memory does not hinge on the present. Accept the reality of pain, and love anyway. Think about how people add to your life. Reach out to people by sending thank you notes. Using time better is a process. Do one small thing better today. All time passes, but some moments transcend the ticking. We simply need to notice, and soon we see more and more.

Title: Stop fixing yourself: wake up, all is well
Author: Anthony de mello
Notes: You have everything you need. You can already be happy. We are programmed from birth to believe that we need things to be happy, things in the future, attributes, etc., to be happy. Our beliefs are false. Want to get rid of your suffering? Drop your false beliefs. Love embraces the whole of life. Your attachments to things drain the love of life. We are programmed to not challenge the programming. Love requires objectivity and observation. You are not deliberately causing yourself unhappiness. Do not blame your programming. Let go of attachment to things and letting them give you happiness or displeasure. It is selfish for others to demand we choose them over ourselves. It is not selfish to achieve your own happiness, to let go of attachments, to not seek pleasure from others. If you let go of your attachments and cravings, you cease to drive with your breaks on. When you love for nothing, you have all your skills and energy, you’re relaxed and you don't care. This is being awakened. No need for praise or things to make you happy. The ancients did not care for honor. Gaming or gaining the world means you lose yourself. Only the adult being is able to be one thing and pretend to be another. The way of self-understanding: learn as much as possible, regardless of the outcome. Non-selective, never rigid, transparent, etc. For the things you fear: this too shall pass away. Happiness is not conscious, experienced. The cause of unhappiness is false belief. Our programming is so strong that we don't have a suspicion that we could be wrong, that we should doubt at all. Most people are in a dream, with no idea they are dreaming. True happiness is not gained or caused, it is a natural state. You don’t experience happiness because you need to drop attachments. Through awareness: observe that a belief is false, and it drops. Awareness. Happiness is a grace, called awareness.  What you are aware of, you are no longer a slave to. When you have attachments, you obsess and seek with earnest, but awareness of this will allow you to drop the attachment. Observe yourself, clearly, without judgment, and experience marvelous changes in self. What should you be aware of? Reactions, relationships. Effortlessly a lover going to their partner, or a hungry man eating. The “effort” is fun, joyful, not toil. No power outside of yourself has the power to make you happy or unhappy. No event justifies a negative feeling. You create the negative feelings based on your programming. Any sorrow for your circumstances is an attachment. Don't identify with your negative feelings. Say “gloominess is there, depression is here”. The harder you try to change yourself, the harder it gets. Don't get tense trying to relax. Don't make a goal of it. Come to reality and let the happiness take care of itself.  You can be happy in your anxiety, or in your depression. How can I make it last? - that’s not happiness, that’s addiction. Serenity prayer. Many things you cannot change. In saying yes to what you cannot change, you are saying yes to God. You will have peace. Perspective: this too will pass away. If what you have is love, hold onto the compassion and matter-of-factness of observing the objective of your attachments, then you will love it and love all else just the same. The orchestra will play a music of its own. Nothing can put it there or take it away. Nothing else will matter anymore. See reality through the eyes of a child. The enlightenment meditation: acceptance let’s feelings surface and dissapate. This can cause pain, but also peace. Only love and understanding can lead to lasting change. Lion parable: the lion believed he was a sheep until he saw his reflection and let out a mighty roar. If we really knew who we are, there wouldn’t be any wars. I can observe the “me”. This is what we think about. Is “i” really changing? Know. I am not my body. We can change the labels without changing the I. Your name, beleifs, etc. are not the I. Do not label. When you are caught up in labels, what value do you have? Labels relate to “me”. Suffering exists in “me”. Children are innocent. They are what they are. Only adults pretend to be something they are not. The world trains then to be something else and hide their true self for so long that they forget it exists and no longer know whi they are. The desire to become is part of this. You are already something. There child surrenders to its nature to be what it is, to live. All you can do is silence the monkey mind and let the heart speak. You have prostitutes yourself for the sake of competition and a goal to become. The world: courting applause and success and fame. If you allow yourself to feel the emptiness of this hell on earth, you may experience pain that would awake you from this slumber. Dare to abandon your teacher and see everything without fear or formula, and see for yourself. If you understand who “I” is, you will be free, fear no one, not care about embarrassment, etc. Life is for the risk taker, not the coward. Those who lose their life shall save it. Those who save it shall lose it. Dead people have an inbuilt fear of change. When you serve, you see. To love is to be sensitive to life and things, persons, responding from sensitivity. Love is not blind. Love is not attachment. Love excludes no one at all, but embraces the whole of life. Your cannot come to possess this kind of love, benevolence for all, who you may not even know. It is already present within you. Remove the blocks you place in front of sensitivity. Blocks of belief, attachment, and fear. Labels cease our seeing, they are beliefs that keep us from seeing. Tension and anxiety removes us from love. Being loved does not cause being loving, but instead euphoria, a temporary switch in the brain. Attempt to see those you love or dislike anew, as if you saw them for the first time. Labels are us seeing through our past. Search for treasures buried at our disposal. See others anew, and see yourself anew. Not judging others will allow you to not judge yourself. Truth is a mystery, and love means seeing the ignorance of all beings, including you. Adopt the mind of a little child, responding to reality, rather than labels that have been programmed into them. You will be appalled to find that your response to others is rarely toward them but instead your programming, beliefs, whether positive or negative. You stereotype to walk with ease, but not with love and understanding and clear thinking. Search for your bias. Charity is pleasure masquerading as self-lessness. A saint is one until he knows it. The worst kind of charity is doing something to avoid a bad feeling. Everything you are irritated with someone or something, look within and say “the cause of this irritation is not them, but me”. How are you causing yourself irritation? Could it be what you are irritated reflects something in your own life, or something in you? Are you irritated because they fail to live up to the standards and expectations that have been programmed into you? Given their life, background, and programming, they cannot help but behave as they do. See this and you will respond with love. How foolish of you to threatening they live up to expectations that your parents programmed into you?  Am I in charge of this situation or is the situation in charge of me? You become in charge when you stop letting the situation cause you irritation from your pgoramming, when you stop responding with programming, not subject to the situation. Irritation will only make you less effective. Search for this person’s defects in yourself, and your anger will turn to gratitude for self-awareness. Being evil is a sickness caused by a lack of consciousness. Before you used to be controlled, now you can see others as opportunities, to avoid no one and to go anywhere. Evil is a lack of awareness, a sickness. Awareness and understanding turns bitterness to compassion. Silence: the first revelation it brings is yourself. It will bring you things no money or influence can, such as peace. As the quality deepens, so will your quietness, and then change. Silence will become power to you. Your ideas of God are all inadequate, they fall short. Look, listen, hear, and see. God dances the world. He is in creation. Beauty is a way of seeing. In the heart. Look at the dance, and perhaps you will recognize the dancer. Suffering is when you clash with reality, out of touch with the truth. Suffering points out that there is falsehood somewhere. Identifying ourselves with anything, is a falsehood, and creates suffering. What leads to growth is painful experiences. If we knew how to use suffering, how we would grow. Observe disappointment, what does it say about you? Every feeling is useful for understanding, for growth. Every painful event contains in it a seed of growth. Whatever causes you painful feelings is a teacher. What does that emotion say about you, or way of life, your perception, your programming? You will suddenly find you are full of gratitude for that event or person that brought in you negative emotions. You will find grace for others. Your causing pain in others is a seed of growth for them. All is growth. Dawn meditation: listen to creation greeting the day. What sentiment do you think creation is expressing as it wakes up? There is a song too in your heart. If you have never heard the song, you have not listened. Listen to your heartworm blending with creation all around you. Give up your dependence on your drug. Though you will not be of the world, you will continue to live in it. You will have nowhere to lay your head. Develop a taste for the good things in life: take on activities you can do with your whole being, where you are so engaged that you care not for approval, success, or recognition. Return to nature and commune with creation. Drop the words and concepts and contact reality. You will become more energetic, alive, etc.

Title: Code Dependent
Author: Madhumita murgia
Notes: AI systems are built to serve needs of the masses, but harm a portion of the group. The issues are not readily apparent in the bay area, but they soon will be. Low wages, dependency, replacement of initial labor with machines, cheap labor, nda, no voice for change, etc. Exploiting impoverished or vulnerable populations. Nightmares from traumatizing content viewed to filter. Lack of agency. Deep fakes, falsified porn, and scams using these technologies. Misogyny, and hypersexualization of women using deep fake algorithms. Fake nudes creation (sexual harassment), as a service. No accountability for inappropriate content on the biggest platforms and companies in the world. Deepfake crime is not recognized by most governments as illegal. Even laws that exist are not strictly adhered to or enforced, and the globalist nature of the internet prevents cracking down on crime. Your identity: no privacy with facial recognition, identity theft, flawed policing, unpermitted surveillance. Authoritarian surveillance. The ethics of building AI systems.  “The Trial”. Harm to random citizens, like Uber drivers unfairly paid or treated. Faulty calculations, and not enough human oversight. Algorithmic discrimination, intentionally or unintentionally. Those harmed can be reluctant to speak up. Human rights issues in how these systems are maintained and governed. Simply looking at violent content can cause PTSD. Many platforms are built on the backs of the most vulnerable. NDAs make people afraid to trust one another, and afraid to speak up. Spying, surveillance, justice systems, governing. Industrial complexes. Social media misinformation spread and virality. Hateful content stays online longer in many countries. Anti-trust law. Mistaken algorithmic attacks in military and warfare. Uyghurs’ oppression. China and surveillance. AI replacing those it was trained on. AI is better named “Applied Statistics”. Anthropomorphizing a stats model is problematic. It feels like there’s someone on the other end, but there’s not. A post-truth world. Eventually people get used to it, and no longer know how to fix “the machine”. The Machine Stops - science fiction book. Silicon valley: move fast and break things. Maybe we don't want so many things to be broken.

Title: Find your why
Author: Simon sinek
Notes: Fulfillment is a right, not a lottery. You should feel inspired at the end of every day. If your organization does not do that for you, then you are responsible for making it happen. Inspire people around you. Fulfillment ≠ happiness. Happiness is fleeting. Fulfillment comes when our work connects directly with our why. Everyone has a why. Happiness comes from what we do. Fulfillment comes from why. Lead woth why, not what or how. Why is more emotionally potent. We are not entirely rational beings. How we feel about something or someone is more powerful than what we think. Feelings are difficult to communicate in words. Golden circle: in a target, what = outer ring, how = middle, why = middle bullseye. Every company, team, and individual has a why. Why is a tool, making the abstract tangible. Discovering your why injects passion into your work. How can you find people who believe who you believe if you don't know your own why, your own beliefs? The why of an org: the founder’s story, or elements of the existing culture. The why is an origin story. Bring out your defining moments, gold in your past, etc. The more specific the memories, the better. The quality of the memory matters. At least 10 memories. Identify fhemes.

Title: The trading game.
Author: Gary stevenson
Notes: Quite enjoyable. Entertaining story for the sake of a story, but can’t say how much seems actually true. entertaining and interesting nonetheless.

Title: Scarcity brain
Author: Michael easter
Notes: Eat one-ingredient foods, not ultra-processed. The scarcity loop: opportunity, unpredictable rewards, quick repeatability. Naturally evolved, from our time of hunting/gathering, etc.

Title: The love prescription
Author: John gottman, Julie Schwartz gottman
Notes: You can avoid sweating the small stuff for some things, but for love, it is all about the small stuff. Love is something you do, and action. Make contact, turn toward bids for connection. Avoid the four horsemen: criticism, contempt, defensiveness, stonewalling. Ask a big question. Say thank you. Give a real compliment. Ask for what you need. Reach out and touch, nonsexually. Declare a date night. People change everyday, we should rediscover who they are throughout our relationship. We will learn things we didn’t know, and things that have changed for them.

Title: Captivate
Author: Vanessa van edwards
Notes: Be authentic, don’t fake it. Emotions are contagious, so step one to being liked and helping others feel great is to only go to events that make you happy, so you don't have to fake it. Create your own rules… 1. play to your position (what are you good at? What fits you? Don’t play center if you’re not tall enough): Places to socialize, your thrive locations: restaurants, phone calls, video chat, nature, backyard BBQ, dinner parties, movie night. Your survive locations are places you dislike. Think of your 3 favorite locations, your thrive locations. Accept invitations or plan events in your thrive locations. 2. Work the room: don’t hover at the start zone, where people are not yet comfortable or willing to open up. The side zone: bathroom, food, people you know. These are traps. The best thing to do is to wave and say hi to friends and tell them you’ll catch them later. Capitalize on your fresh energy. The social zone: “where people exit the bar”, where they are ready to mingle, where the host can introduce you, the couch or bartable. Be a grader, take breaks between “courses” in the meal. Go for the appetizer, main course, dessert, etc. 3. Know your team: who do you love spending time with? Who makes you laugh? Who do you most look forward to seeing? Who do you wish you could get to know better? Who do you go to for strategizing? Who makes you feel valued? Who do you call in a crisis? Who makes you feel like your best self? Your winger: helps you feel comfortable and shares your goals for growth. Your riser: someone you wish was on this list. Rely on the people that help you thrive. You do not have to like everyone. Say no, you will remember who you are. Take control, play to your strengths. Challenge: say no to an event you are dreading. At your next event, find two sweet spots, identify someone as your riser. Reach out to a winger and invite them to socialize. Don’t socialize in ways that drain you. How to make a killer first-impression: people make first impressions in 2 seconds. This is to your advantage. Use your hands, posture, and eyes. Hands out of pockets. Keep hands visible. Pockets are murderers of rapoir. Shake their hand like a testing a peach. Stop squeezing, when you feel their muscles. Releasing Oxytocin helps people decide you are a friend, not foe. When we are proud, we want people to notice us, so we take up space. Use the launch stance. We sometimes move into loser stance by checking our phone. Avoid checking your phone before important meetings, etc. Do something else. Stand like a winner. Engage with eye contact, showing a desire for alliance. Experience along with others. Talking with or to, not at. Hold eye contact 60% of the time, to create trust, use gaze to produce connection. We look at people we like. If someone looks at another, the other will start to like the first. Holding eye contact calls on courage, and produces Oxytocin. When you like someone you look at them more. In most cultures, gaze helps others begin to like us. In the first few seconds, avoid the temptation to look away shyly. Big talk: skirting norms,  challenging chitchat status quo. Emotional peaks, or sparks. Use unique talking points to create pleasurable and memorable conversations. Sparks are marked by dopamine, excitement, and dopamine helps your memory, like a post-it note to remember. Dopemine in a conversation increases your memorability. 1. Sparkers:

Title: Creativity, Inc.
Author: Ed catmull
Notes:
Intro:
Many businesses create a big bubble and pop when they start getting funding and enter hypergrowth and get lots of attention
• Why do leaders not know how to manage growth?
He set out to learn how to manage well as Pixar gained attention after Toy Story film
We start from the presumption that our people are talented and want to contribute.
[Using self-fulfilling? Pygmalion effect]
Everybody has the potential to be creative.
Blocks get in the way. There are steps to protect the creative process.
Mechanisms: deal with uncertainty, instability, lack of candor, and the things we cannot see.
Make room for what we do not know [unknown unknowns]
Embrace the idea that their models may be wrong or incomplete.
Pay attention to and engage with anything that creates fear.
Trust people they work with.
—---------
The long table created separation and undermined their own principles.
Leaders didn't feel excluded, so they figured others didn't. Others figured it was intentional. It created habits like “place cards” that were there even after the table was gone.
A solution is a multi-step endeavor.
• The problem you know you were trying to solve
• The other problems, saplings, that remain even after you cut the oak tree down.
—-------------
Disney - create the new
Einstein - explain what already is
Peter pan, Cinderella, lady and the tramp.
• Disney was inventing technologies of their own. They developed the tools to perfect color, etc.
• They talked about it on their show.
Animation is successful when it is a living, feeling entity.
Grew up in Utah, felt anything was possible.
ARPA - response to sputnik.
• Advanced research projects agency (now DARPA).
He liked that idea - “we'll just get smarter”.
He loved drawing. Went to school for computer languages. Met a man who told him about a program that could use and rotate illustrated objects, etc.
The people he was with were great.
Had the genius that worked amazingly on their own
Had the group that excelled because of their multiplicity of views
ARPAnet. Funded by ARPA.
They trusted those they sponsored to innovate.
As graduate students, they felt like they could invent and learn.
His dream was growing, with a new goal: to animate with a computer. It spoke to both of his dreams.
He started the challenge of drawing a human hand with polygons, etc. on a computer. A real challenge, no flat edges, etc. And then to make it move, a bigger challenge.
They didn't know what was impossible.
Made a formal exchange between Disney and Utah university. Trade stories for animation.
Subdivision of surfaces: divide the surfaces into different pieces. Texture mapping.
Z-buffer. Depth to every object in a space.
Computer memory was limited.
The leaders of the department had created a laboratory, protective space, a place to inspire.
How to get into another space like this?
No company or university shared his goal of creating a feature film.
• Received a call from new york institute of technology.
• Alex was starting a research lab to bring computers into the process. He was a visionary. Funded the project. He brought Ed in to assemble a team.
• First interviewee seemed more qualified than Ed was. He hired him anyway.
    ◦ To get the greatest minds, he had to put his own insecurities away.
• Made a policy of always hiring people that are smarter than he is. Always take a chance on better.
• Created a flat org structure. Trusted everyone to be self-motivated.
• Inventing simulated motion blur. They published their work and went to conferences. Made lots of valuable relationships and connections.
• Big studios refused to get in on animation.
Never stop questioning
Starwars changed this.
George Lucas.
• Film and tech. Special effects.
• Ed went to Lucas Film to interview.
• They asked him who else would be good for the job. He seemed to get the job because, unlike his peers that didn't recommend anyone, he did. He was seen as confident. Hired for his honesty, clarity, vision.
• George wanted to do a big project. It couldn't be like a research lab with individual projects.
• He hired people as managers and had them report to him.
• Silicon Valley. Great environment for this.
• They were going to create video editing.
    ◦ But people were resistant to change at Lucasfilm.
• Needed buy-in. Managers needed to engender support for ideas among the people charged with employing them.
    ◦ Influence. Managing was hard. Books were lacking in content. George did it much like yoda, with folksy ideas. Do or do not, there is not try.
• George idealized the process of moving toward something.
    ◦ He bet on himself. Instead of getting a raise, he asked for retaining rights to merchandising, etc. 
Steve jobs took control, assertive.
john lassater - fired from Disney the next day for pitching the brave little toaster. A bit too avant garde.
• Creativity had been stifled at Disney. Hierarchy and status were valued. No new tech since 101 Dalmatians. Lost knack for innovation.
• George brought his creativity to lucasfilm/Pixar to create real emotion and story.
• Story is more important than flawless execution and perfect graphics, etc.
Responsibility for finding and solving problems is given to every person at every level of the process. - the people who work closest to the problem.
Ask the fundamental questions, not the surface-level questions.
Steve sized up the world by sending out impulses, harsh thoughts, and seeing how others responded.
He respected passion.
Story is king
Trust the process
Ideas come from people.
Get good people to make good things
The process depends on people.
…………
“The brain trust” - group of people meets together with candor to solve problems. Not too big. Known for storytelling skill.
[They trust each others’ brains, and thus as a whole they are a brain that can be trusted]
The brain trust has no authority.
Separate ideas from people and self.
Additive candor.
• Sometimes the Braintrust finds a problem but addresses the wrong symptom or cause.
Speaking the truth is the only way to yield quality.
If people are holding back, sometimes a smaller braintrust is held to hopefully get them to open up.
Creating a braintrust is something that evolves over time. And people have to understand the philosophy of the trust.
• People you choose must
    ◦ Make you feel smarter
    ◦ Put lots of solutions on the table in a short amount of time
You don't want to be at a company where there is more candor in the hallways than in rooms where ideas are hashed out.
Once you find these people, hold onto them.
………………..
Most people don't want to fail.
But fail fast.
Trying to avoid failure leads to inevitable failure and trouble.
We aren't very good at predicting the future.
Failure is an agent of learning.
Ask yourself, “what happens when an error is discovered?” - true test of company culture around failure.
“Who's fault is this?” - vilifying failure
Loosen fear’s grip on your company. Create a fearless culture by bias toward action and not shaming failure.
If you decide you're in the wrong place, there is still time to move toward the right place.
All the thinking that led you down that alley was not wasted. Explore the neighborhood. What you like may spawn ideas later.
Any outcome is a good outcome because it yields new information.
If you seek to plot out all your moves, you're planning to be unoriginal.
The more time you spend mapping out an approach, the more you become attached to it.
…………………
Stop doing things that might fail = no innovation
Being too risk averse is the beginning of irrelevance.
They took on a project and shut it down. Worth it.
The braintrust represents the audience.
If the crew is confused, the leader is probably confused too
• The crew is a reliable barometer
The failure is a failure of many
• The event itself
• Our reaction
    ◦ The part we control
    ◦ How do we react?
        ▪ Remember failure is a chance to grow
Leaders should be teachers
• Do we think of most activities as learning/teaching opportunities?
Uncouple fear and failure
• Messaging you send to managers
    ◦ Remove the “do great work and support your people” + “oh and make sure everything goes smoothly”
Managers typically want two things
• Everything to be in-control
• For them to appear in-control
• These are time wasters
    ◦ You start to avoid surprises, and that means people walk on eggshells
How to avoid time wasted, and increase trust?
• Candidness
• Give people ownership over information
    ◦ By sharing information with employees, employees become shared partners - they don’t want to share secrets with the outside world
“I was afraid of failure”
• What changed?
    ◦ Experience weathering failure
Forget your model of what you “should” be
• The job is never what you think it is
• Look at people on your team, see how they are working together
    ◦ Can they rally together in the face of a problem?
        ▪ If yes, you are succeeding
How to prove to employees that you don’t stigmatize failure?
• You get worried if you don’t have problems
Management’s job is not to prevent risk, but to build the ability to recover
—---------------------------------
Disney: feed the beast. An assembly-line method for creation. Lessens quality across the board.
The bulk of the people still had the talent and drive, but the beast led out and had to be fed.
Originality is fragile. The ugly baby (original ideas in infancy) don't coexist well with the beast. They need to be protected at first. Legal departments are famous for being overly protective of the status quo, the assembly line.
Protect the new, the original idea, what is not entrenched. Protect from people who don't understand that in order for greatness to emerge, it must come from ungreatness.
A large portion of our cost: we didn't stop tinkering.
• Goal became: finalize the script before we started building.
• Finding Nemo ended up becoming as tinkery as other movies. It was also super successful.
• Efficiency is not the goal. Product/creation is.
Reality lies somewhere between the beast and the baby.
Any group that drives revenue could be considered the beast. The baby has unknown needs and unexpected turns. Neither is all bad or good. A balance.
The beast is not individual people. It's the system.
No creative business is immune.
There must be sufficient push back against the beast. Balance.
Each group is under pressure to perform well, not thinking about their effect on other groups. If any group wins, “we” lose. Need competing desires, but balance.
Every creative organization is an echo system.
View conflict as essential. To see conflict as healthy.
A good manager must always be on the lookout for where balance has been lost.
There isn't any other way to learn than by doing.
Values remain consistent, but goals can shift as needed.
Culture that protects the new.
Protecting the new is not isolating the new. We don't polish bricks.
People are more important than ideas.
Greenlight: point in a hollywood project when a studio decides it is a viable film.
Internships are mechanisms for spotting talent and seeing if outsiders fit in.
Interns helped people see how they did things.
Interns program needed protection at first, but then didn't as it became established.
Business in general does not need protection. You don't need to protect the beast.
Anton ego: the world is often unkind to new talent, new creations. The new needs friends.
……………………………………
You can't avoid change. You shouldn't want to.
People want to hang on to things that have worked.
It is because of the inevitability of change that people hold on to what they know.
Change will happen whether you like it or not.
Randomness is part of the beauty of life. Make choices to see unpredictable for what it is, and let it work for us.
Sometimes you can pretend and say “if we did this, just pretend, then what if…”
The creative process is expensive. Shunning necessary investment impedes creativity.
The person who can't change their mind - that's danger.
Lack of change and unexpectedness should cause worry.
Why would anyone embrace change?
Once you master any system, you typically become blind to its flaws.
Don't change for change sake. Much of bureaucracy was put in place for reason. But many rules in aggregate may only accomplish one thing: drain creative impulse.
Randomness remains stubbornly difficult to understand.
Our brains are made to find patterns, even when they are not there. We're not built for seeking randomness.
We ignore the things we cannot see.
Difficult for us to see between chance and skill.
We form patterns of thinking based on experience. We can't see the alternatives that might have happened.
When companies are successful, they misattribute. Randomness and luck played a large part.
Be careful not to believe your own hype.
Physics: occam's razor. We believe the simpler something is, the more fundamental or true it is. Not everything is simple. The simple explanation is so desirable, but we must face the unknown.
The unknown is not our enemy in creativity.
We tend to apply our skills we are good at to areas they do not apply in.
Stochastic self-similarity. We are quick to assign patterns later, but we don't see them coming.
Randomness does not happen in a vacuum.
Big and small problems are self-similar, not separate problems to be isolated.
Randomness created their data loss, but also their data recovery.
Always walk your talk. If all our careful planning can't prevent problems, then best method of response is to enable employees at every level to own the problems and have the confidence to fix them. Feel like they can fix problems without asking permission. Improvisation created the backup at home that saved toy story 2.
There are too many problems to solve.
If we allow more people to solve problems without permission, The org is not frozen waiting for approval, problems get fixed faster.
We don't always know which bucket to put a problem in. Instead push those problems down into the organization, and let the unpredictable potential of humans work its magic.
Everyone says they want to hire excellent people. No one knows who will really rise up to make a difference.
Walt disney was never matched. People asked “what would want do?” and ended up stuck in the past.
Acknowledge random events, and luck, and stroke of fortune.
Work with change - what creativity is about.
…………………………
“The hidden”:
• We are going to fail bad, we don't know when or how. We should prepare for a hidden problem we cannot see.
• Be aware you have unknown problems. Try to uncover what is unseen.
• What we see and know is inevitability flawed. Some problems will always be hidden from you.
Even if we learned every discipline, we would still have blind spots.
Try to understand the many reasons why something might be difficult or impossible to see.
Different levels:
• Promotion to leadership: access to information changes when people see you as a leader.
• Hierarchy: people often focus on managing upward and ignoring those beneath them, because they focus on status/rank. They become skilled at finding what a leader wants.
• Even employees with the purest intentions may be too timid to bring up issues/problems.
• We draw conclusions based on incomplete information. Becomes even more difficult when you are successful, because you think you are doing well.
Ideas are additive
A culture that acknowledges its own blindspots.
We are two inches from things not happening.
We think success is inevitable.
The history would be very different if things didn't happen how they did. Much is hidden from us, out of our sight. Be truly humble, because many factors in your business are out of sight.
Hindsight is not 20/20, anymore than our view of the future.
The past is our teacher, not our master. We are usually not aware that our recollection of past Memories is highly selective.
The actual amount of information before our eyes is vast. We take in a little, and fill in the majority with our brain.
We are reading micro expressions and small movements with people.
The illusion that we have a complete picture of reality is extraordinarily persuasive.
We create the illusion, but are unaware of the process.
The models we have about other people, society, etc., shape how we see.
We have personal models, shaped by our experience.
When humans see things that challenge our mental models, we tend not just to resist them but ignore them.
• Confirmation bias - lesser weight to data that contradicts what we believe is true.
• Words from those close to us will sink in while a stranger's words are ignored.
Our mental models are not reality. They are tools we use. Like a model for forecasting weather. The tool is not reality.
Making a movie… the unmade future.
• Making something out of nothing is difficult.
People who eagerly embrace the unknown: through questioning they can do more than look through a door, they can venture across.
Others who venture but have little awareness of what they have done. They are successful but stay on the side of the known.
What stands in our way are hidden barriers. We must acknowledge it. We can't cling to what works, fearing change, deluding ourselves about what works or does not.
Candor, safety, research, protecting the new.
Uncover hidden problems.
.……………….
Broadening our view:
Models: preconceptions we have built up over time. They distort our world and make it hard to see what's in front of us.
We don't typically see the boundary between nee info and old established mental models
When we unknowingly get caught up in our own interpretations, we become inflexible.
People that work or live together, have by virtue or proximity and shared history, models of the world that are deeply or sometimes hopelessly tied together. This effect multiplies quickly in an organization.
As more people are added to any group, there is an inexorable drift toward inflexibility.
Mental rigidity can be difficult to recognize.
Mechanisms: we are trying to convince ourselves to challenge our preconceptions.
1. Daily's or solving problems together
2. Research trips
3. The power of limits
4. Integrating tech and art
5. Short experiments
6. Learning to see
7. Post mortems
8. Continuing to learn
Daily's
Detailed analysis.
People join with preset expectations. Teach them that everyone makes mistakes. Everyone shows incomplete work. Everyone is free to make suggestions. When embarrassment goes away, people become more creative. Magnified by the people around you = people see more clearly
Research trips
Cutting up what's come before appears to be safe, and is a guaranteed path to mediocrity. Craft without art
Craft: what we are expected to know.
Art: the unexpected use of our craft.
We're after authenticity
Go out and do research. You never stumble upon the unexpected if you stick only to the familiar. 
Research trips challenge your preconceptions and keep cliches at bay. They fuel inspiration and what keeps us creating rather than copying.
Authenticity comes through always.
Very few viewers have been in a high-end French restaurant kitchen. But it's not lost on the audience, they can tell.
No detail is too small.
The power of limits
We care about every detail. The beautifully shaded penny. Desire for quality can go well beyond rationality.
How do you fix this problem without telling people to not worry about it or be less excellent?
How do you set limits as management?
The limits imposed internally: you can't do everything you want, so we must think of smarter ways to work. Limits force us to rethink how we work and push to new heights of creativity. Unless you impose limits, people will spend more money and time, because a movie's demand for resources is bottomless.
People care about their piece, and don't always see how it fits into the whole.
Mirage: task that leads you along and doesn't add any real value.
System to avoid: popsicle sticks stuck to wall. Each stick represented a person's week. A glance at the wall would tell you opportunity cost and the limited time. If you need more time, you have to take the stick from somewhere.
How do we enable our people to solve problems… rather than, how do we prevent our people from screwing up?
Integrating tech and art
Art challenges technology and technology inspires art.
Pixar short films: experiments, meant to push tech boundaries, r and d. But they ended up not pushing those boundaries but gave other benefits. They reaffirmed their values of creativity. Also served as a prototyping task, easy to mess up story on a short.
Left and right brain. 
Data is one way of seeing. You can't measure many things.
To learn to draw, you have to turn off the right brain or something, see the space around an object, see objects instead of images, etc. Learn to suppress the part of the brain that jumps to conclusions. Place a shoe upside down and your brain will see the true form, not place a preformed image on top of it or project an image. Draw the space around an chair and it's proportions are likely more correct. Look at different points in a lake as opposed to the whole and you'll see many colors, not the blue that your mind fills in when seeing the whole. Art is about learning to see. Learn to temporarily suspend the habits and impulses that obscure your vision. Draw the unchair.
Beginner's mind, a startup mentality.
Postmortems: switching it up each time, doing midmortems, etc. Because people get used to things, don't always like feedback, and learn how to game the system.
The future
The best way to predict the future is to invent it
Your movie or project will start to tell you what it needs to be.
Temptation to use everything you find or excavate during the process, even if it doesn't fit.
Making a movie can be like an archeological dig. You don't know what you're looking for.
That said, you are not necessarily uncovering something that existed before, you are creating something new. Some people need to believe that it exists to be uncovered.
Like climbing a mountain blindfolded. A mountain is not always upward climb, you have no way of knowing what comes.
The untreated is a vast space: this scares most people. They need a mental models. Most models have a common thread of a search for the unknown.
It's not driving the train, it's laying the tracks.
Mindfulness: the search for a clear mind is one of the main goals of all creative people.
Mindfulness helps us make peace with what we cannot control, remain open to knew ideas, and deal with our problems squarely.
The brain tends to suppress problems instead of dealing with them directly.
People with mindful practice don't ignore the pain, their mind increases pain threshold. They feel it and see it for what it is, but the mind lessens the response to it so it can cope and not overthink.
Don't hang on too tightly to the past or future. Live in the present.
Testing what we know
A knew challenge
Taking over disney animation: would these theories work there too?
Refused contracts, a risk for disney and a risk for Pixar joining a bureaucracy. A situation requiring reciprocal trust.
Disney desks/cubicles: sterile and impersonal. They had cleared desks to make a good impression. There was an inordinate emphasis on preventing errors. 
John and ed: ripped out some walls, put carpet in to direct to their office. Took down shades/blinds. Trying their best to make it a space of candor and invitation.
Started by assuming leaders were trained wrong, not incompetent.
Had to change incentives. Directors had been competing for resources.
Kept Disney and Pixar separate. No production work for each other.
Curiosity was what made Disney's great leaders during this time.
Woman drafted a huge plan. He said it's like a pyramid. It will narrow opportunities, your mind will focus only on that. Instead, be open to where you need to go.
Disney had an informal undercover braintrust story group, but they now needed a formal braintrust.
They embraced the idea, but it would be a while before it came naturally.
They had to learn trust, had to learn that they were beating the project not each other. They had to unlearn being a teacher's pet to the leader.
Princess and the frog: 2d, and incorporated research trips for the first time to Disney teams.
Tangled was a huge success for disney. Moving toward the future rather than holding to the past.
Easy isn't the goal, quality is.
Gifted personal notes and bonuses, shaking each hand and saying thank you after the tangled film success.
The principles applied to disney worked. Most fo the people were still there and learned a new way of working.
Small teams with autonomy
Notes day
Responding to crisis.
Our problem, what “we” can do to solve it together.
Leadership gathered. Two items: rising cost of making films, and change in culture with growth.
People were under tremendous pressure not to fail. They were beginning to avoid risk.
Personal project days: twice a month, spend a day doing anything you want. Doesn't have to contribute to a Pixar film/project. Personal time to explore.
Give them the time, and they come up with the ideas.
Notes day: a day for solving the problem of cost/culture, but letting the people solve it. Asking the teams to give solutions and brainstorm. They are in the weeds.
What they wanted most? Do more with less. An efficient time budget movie, an exciting challenge.
Scourge of entitlement. Need to understand others’ roles, the different parts of the company and processes, to see others as peers, etc.
Notes day worked because it had a clear and common goal, was championed by leadership, and was led from within. The people made it happen.
We continue to figure it out, to persist.
The future is not a destination, it's a direction. Our work is never done.
Unleashing creativity = loosen our controls, accept risk, trust colleagues, work to clear a path for them, pay attention to anything that creates fear. Ease isn't the goal, excellence is.
……………………
Steve jobs: passion as part of his logic
Steve had the skill of a director: strong and complete will when committed to an idea, but openness to changing beliefs and getting feedback.

Title: Never split the difference
Author: Chris voss
Notes:
The new rules
Your sons on the line.
• There’s always a bit of panic
The open-ended question: it has no clear answer
• Buys you time
• People have to then negotiate with themselves. It wears them down if they are relentless, and makes them consider if they won’t
Do techniques work with normal humans? Yes, every interaction, everywhere
We are all essentially monkeys, but there is no sequence. You may do A, E, and then Q
Hostages have existed since the beginning of time
• Until recently, it was solved with brute force
New York police put together a negotiation tactics project
Harvard Negotiation Project - Getting to yes
• Systemize problem solving
    ◦ Rational problem solving
        ▪ Separate person/emotion from problem
        ▪ Don’t get wrapped up in their position, but focus on their interests
        ▪ Work cooperatively to generate win-win options
        ▪ Establish mutually agreed upon standards for evaluating those solutions

• We’re afraid of not getting along with the rest of the tribe
Navigate it with empathy
Ignore the genie that tells you to give up or run, or yell, etc.
The adversary is the situation
Use conflict to get the situation going without stumbling into battle
• Pushing hard for what you believe is not selfish, bullying, just helping you
• If you are an honest decent person, looking for a reasonable outcome, you can ignore the amygdala. You are trying to uncover value. Not strongarming or pigeonholing
• You are demanding creativity, pushing toward a solution
Don’t avoid honest clear conflict
• It will get you the best price
• It will save your marriage, family, etc.
Be honest about what one can and cannot do.
What we don’t know can kill us or a deal, but uncovering it can totally change a negotiation and bring unexpected success
We don’t know the question to ask for fleshing out black swans, because we can’t predict them
• Let what you know guide you but not blind you
• Black swans are leverage multipliers
    ◦ Positive - ability to give them what they want
    ◦ Negative - ability to hurt them
    ◦ Normative - using their norms to bring them around
• Work to understand their religion - their life, emotional and otherwise
• Review everything you hear from them
• Exploit the similarity principle - dig for what makes them tick and show you share common ground
• When they seem irrational or crazy, they most likely aren’t. Search for constraints, hidden desires, and bad information
• Get face time. Pay attention to their verbal and nonverbal communication before and after, and things that seem out of line
Prepare a Negotiation One-Sheet
Goal:
• Identify specific scenario that represents best case.
• Set an optimistic but reasonable goal and define it clearly.
• Write it down.
• Discuss your goal with a colleague (creates commitment and consistency).
• Carry the written goal into the negotiation.
Summary:
• A couple of sentences about the known facts that have led up to the negotiation. Intended to produce a that’s right response.
3-5 Labels to Perform an Accusation Audit:
• It seems like [] is valuable to you.
• It seems like you don’t like []
• It seems like you value []
• It seems like [] makes it easier.
• It seems like you’re reluctant to []
3-5 Calibrated Questions to Reveal Value and Overcome Potential Deal Killers:
For your counterpart:
• What are we trying to accomplish?
• How is that worthwhile?
• What’s the core issue here?
• How does that affect things?
• How does this fit into what the objective is?
To identify behind-the-table deal killers:
• How does this affect the rest of your team?
• How on board are the people not on this call?
• What do your colleagues see as their main challenges in this area?
To identify and diffuse deal-killing issues:
• What are we up against here?
• What is the biggest challenge you face?
• How does making a deal with us affect things?
• What happens if you do nothing?
• What does doing nothing cost you?
• How does making this deal resonate with what your company prides itself on?
3-5 Labels to Follow Up After They Answer Your Calibrated Question:
• It seems like [] is important.
• It seems you feel like my company is in a unique position to []
• It seems you are worried that []
Non-cash offers:
• List of non-cash items possessed by your counterpart that would be valuable to you.
• What could they give you that would make you do this for free?

Notes: Love and kindness are gifts, not deserved. Therefore we can be grateful for them. We don’t need to feel unjustly dealt with when others are unkind, because that is to be expected. Respond with compassion. It is a gift to have received love. We must live our life as we see fit. There is no need to worry about losing others’ kindness and love, because it was never ours to hold or control anyway, it was extra beauty and joy in our life. Live a life true to you, not what others expect you to do. You cannot control their affection. Conflict is inevitable in all families and groups. Lack of outward conflict is not the same thing as fulfilling connection and earned peace. Regret 1: I wish I'd had the courage to live a life true to myself, not the one others expected of me. It is a beautiful thing to see others living true to themselves. Be happy for them. Love them for not having to others’ expectations.  We are products of our environment.
